facts.headline: Marcel Balsa is born
facts.detail: One time French F1 driver, Emanuel Marcel Lucien Balsa, was born in Saint-Frion, France.

facts.headline: Hap Sharp is born
facts.detail: James "Hap" Sharp, co-owner and founder of Chaparral Cars, is born in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

facts.headline: Pedro Rodriguez wins the South African Grand Prix
facts.detail: Mexican F1 driver, Pedro Rodriguez, wins his first career F1 race at Kyalami for Cooper-Maserati.

facts.headline: Beppe Gabbiani is born
facts.detail: Beppe Gabbiani, who participated in 17 GPs, was born in Piacenza, Italy.

facts.headline: Michael Schumacher is born
facts.detail: Seven-time World Champion Michael Schumacher was born in Hürth-Hermülheim, West Germany.

facts.headline: First African-American driver test-drives an F1 car
facts.detail: Willy T. Ribbs became the first African-American to test an F1 car. He would go on to be the first African-American to compete in the Indy 500.

facts.headline: Mexican Grand Prix cancelled
facts.detail: The Mexican Grand Prix was dropped from the 1971 calendar following crowd control issues and dangerous spectator behaviour during the 1970 race.

facts.headline: Cadillac announces first reserve driver
facts.detail: Cadillac officially announces Zhou Guanyu as their reserve driver for their first season in F1.

facts.headline: Andre Simon is born
facts.detail: Andre Simon, who competed in 12 races for 4 different teams, is born in Paris, France.

facts.headline: Tag Heuer replaces Rolex as the official timekeeper of F1
facts.detail: F1 announces Tag Heuer as official F1 timekeeper, ending the 11-year relationship with Rolex.

facts.headline: Lewis Hamilton is born
facts.detail: Seven-time World Champion Lewis Hamilton was born in Stevenage, England.

facts.headline: Tom Delaney is born
facts.detail: Cyril Terence "Tom" Delaney, recognized as the world's oldest racing driver, was born in Willesden, North London.

facts.headline: Maria Teresa de Filippis passes away
facts.detail: Maria Teresa de Filippis, the first female to ever compete in F1, passed away in Scanzorosciate, Italy.

facts.headline: 1977 F1 season kicks off
facts.detail: The 1977 F1 season kicked off at the Argentine Grand Prix, with Jody Scheckter taking P1.

facts.headline: Ignazio Giunti dies
facts.detail: Former Ferrari driver Ignazio Giunti was tragically killed while racing at the 1000km of Buenos Aires, the opening race of the 1971 World Sportscar Championship season.

facts.headline: Eddie Cheever is born
facts.detail: Eddie Cheever, who holds the record for most F1 races participated in as an American, is born in Phoenix, Arizona.

facts.headline: Carroll Shelby is born
facts.detail: Unsuccessful F1 driver, but legendary car designer, Carroll Shelby is born in Leesburg, Texas.

facts.headline: Tom Belso passes away
facts.detail: Tom Belso, Denmark's first ever F1 driver, passes away after battling stomach cancer.

facts.headline: Toto Wolff is born
facts.detail: Mercedes F1 team principal and CEO, Toto Wolff, is born in Vienna, Austria.

facts.headline: 1975 season kicks off in Argentina
facts.detail: The 1975 season kicked off in Argentina, with McLaren Ford driver Emerson Fittipaldi taking the checkered flag.

facts.headline: Juan Manuel Fangio wins his home Grand Prix
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio wins his home Grand Prix in Buenos Aires, beginning the journey to his 5th and final world title.

facts.headline: Denny Hulme wins his final race
facts.detail: Former F1 Champion Denny Hulme wins his last ever race in F1 at the season-opening Argentine Grand Prix.

facts.headline: Dan Gurney passes away
facts.detail: F1 legend and All American Racers founder Dan Gurney died aged 86. He remains the only American driver to win a Grand Prix in a car of his own construction.

facts.headline: Giancarlo Fisichella is born
facts.detail: Giancarlo Fisichella was born in Rome. Across 231 Grands Prix from 1996 to 2009, he took three wins and 19 podiums, including a win with Jordan and two with Renault.

facts.headline: Narain Karthikeyan is born
facts.detail: Narain Karthikeyan, India's pioneering F1 driver, was born in Chennai. He raced for Jordan and later HRT, and famously finished fourth at the chaotic 2005 US Grand Prix.

facts.headline: Mario Andretti dominates the season-opening Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Andretti took his tenth career pole for Lotus and won by over thirty seconds ahead of reigning champion Niki Lauda, launching his run to the 1978 Drivers' Championship.

facts.headline: FIA bans driver aids
facts.detail: FIA chief Max Mosley banned several driver aids including traction control, launch control, and in-race telemetry and radio communication -- though the change was partially reversed within a week.

facts.headline: William Grover-Williams is born
facts.detail: French-British driver William Grover-Williams was born; he won the first-ever Monaco Grand Prix in 1929, then became a WWII resistance hero before being executed by the Nazis in 1945.

facts.headline: Fangio wins the 1955 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio won a gruelling, heat-plagued Argentine GP for Mercedes, suffering burns to his leg from the hot chassis that left a permanent scar.

facts.headline: A.J. Foyt is born
facts.detail: Indy racing legend A.J. Foyt, the first four-time Indy 500 winner, was born; he made three F1 starts at the Indianapolis 500 while it counted toward the World Championship.

facts.headline: Fangio wins a controversial 1954 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio won for Maserati after Ferrari's protest over his pit stop -- claiming too many mechanics worked on his car -- was rejected by race organisers and the FIA.

facts.headline: Team Lotus withdraws from F1
facts.detail: Lotus, winner of six Drivers' and seven Constructors' titles since 1958, announced its withdrawal from Formula 1 due to financial troubles.

facts.headline: Michael Schumacher and Ferrari meet the Pope
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher and the Ferrari team presented Pope John Paul II with a scale model of their 2004 title-winning car during a Vatican visit.

facts.headline: Gilles Villeneuve is born
facts.detail: Legendary Ferrari driver Gilles Villeneuve was born in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Canada; his son Jacques later became F1's 1997 World Champion.

facts.headline: Ascari dominates a tragic 1953 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari led every lap for Ferrari at F1's first-ever Argentine round, a race marred by a crowd invasion of the track that killed 13 spectators.

facts.headline: Pedro Rodriguez is born
facts.detail: Mexican driver Pedro Rodriguez, known for his fearless style, was born; he won for Cooper in 1967 and BRM in 1970 before his death racing sports cars in 1971.

facts.headline: Stirling Moss wins the 1958 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Driving a privately entered Cooper, Stirling Moss passed defending champion Fangio on lap 35 to win -- the first championship victory for a rear-engined car.

facts.headline: Jenson Button is born
facts.detail: 2009 World Champion Jenson Button was born in Frome, England, going on to win the title with Brawn GP.

facts.headline: Ferrari commits to F1 through 2012
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone secured Ferrari's commitment to Formula One through 2012 in a deal reported to be worth $150 million, amid rumours of a rival breakaway series.

facts.headline: Jack Doohan is born
facts.detail: Jack Doohan, Australian F1 driver and son of MotoGP champion Mick Doohan, was born.

facts.headline: Sid Watkins retires as FIA medical delegate
facts.detail: After 26 years advancing trackside medicine, Professor Sid Watkins -- Ayrton Senna's close friend -- announced his retirement.

facts.headline: Jolyon Palmer is born
facts.detail: Jolyon Palmer, son of 1980s F1 driver Jonathan Palmer, was born; he later raced for Renault and became an F1 broadcaster.

facts.headline: Jacques Laffite wins a dramatic 1979 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Laffite took pole, fastest lap, and victory for Ligier in a race marked by an eight-car pileup at the first corner.

facts.headline: Williams almost left off 1994 entry list
facts.detail: Defending champions Williams were initially excluded from the season-opener entry list amid a contract dispute, before rival teams agreed to let them compete.

facts.headline: Reigning champion Mike Hawthorn dies in a road crash
facts.detail: Mike Hawthorn, F1's first British World Champion, was killed in a road accident in Surrey at 29, weeks after retiring from racing.

facts.headline: Fangio wins the 1956 Argentine GP in a borrowed car
facts.detail: After engine trouble, Juan Manuel Fangio took over teammate Luigi Musso's Ferrari mid-race and drove it to victory.

facts.headline: Lewis Hamilton drives a Ferrari for the first time
facts.detail: Hamilton tested the 2023 Ferrari SF-23 at Fiorano ahead of his 2025 move to the team, calling it one of the best feelings of his life.

facts.headline: Jackie Stewart wins the 1972 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Stewart dominated from the start in his Tyrrell to claim his 19th career win in scorching heat.

facts.headline: Driver boycott nearly cancels the 1982 South African GP
facts.detail: Drivers boycotted practice over new super-licence contract terms; after a last-minute deal, Alain Prost won for Renault as Niki Lauda returned from a two-year retirement to finish fourth.

facts.headline: Eddie Irvine announces his F1 retirement
facts.detail: Eddie Irvine retired after failing to secure a 2003 seat, ending a career that included stints at Jordan, Ferrari, and Jaguar.

facts.headline: Jenson Button becomes youngest British F1 driver
facts.detail: At 20, Jenson Button signed with Williams and surpassed Stirling Moss's record as the youngest British driver in F1.

facts.headline: Eddie Jordan sells his F1 team
facts.detail: Eddie Jordan finalised the sale of the Jordan team to the Midland Group after 35 years in motor racing.

facts.headline: Niki Lauda dominates the 1976 Brazilian Grand Prix
facts.detail: The reigning champion won by 21.5 seconds for Ferrari in the season opener, while pole-sitter James Hunt retired late with a sticking throttle.

facts.headline: Rookie Lewis Hamilton crashes at 185mph in testing
facts.detail: Just 11 days into driving an F1 car, Hamilton spun off and hit a tyre wall during pre-season testing in Spain, but was unhurt.

facts.headline: Luca Badoer is born
facts.detail: Luca Badoer, born in Treviso, became Ferrari's long-serving test driver and made a surprise return to racing at 38 in 2009 as Felipe Massa's injury replacement.

facts.headline: David Purley is born
facts.detail: British driver David Purley was born; in only his second F1 race he tried to rescue Roger Williamson from a burning car, earning the George Medal for bravery.

facts.headline: Carlos Pace wins his only F1 race, at home in Brazil
facts.detail: Pace took his sole Grand Prix victory in front of 80,000 fans at the 1975 Brazilian GP, with countryman Emerson Fittipaldi charging to second.

facts.headline: Sergio Perez is born
facts.detail: Sergio Perez, who went on to win six Grands Prix and finish runner-up in the 2023 championship, was born in Guadalajara, Mexico.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi wins a rain-shortened 1974 Brazilian Grand Prix
facts.detail: Heavy rain forced the race to be stopped after 31 of 40 laps, handing Emerson Fittipaldi his first win with McLaren.

facts.headline: Rene Arnoux wins the 1980 Brazilian Grand Prix
facts.detail: Arnoux took his first career win for Renault after teammate Jean-Pierre Jabouille's early lead ended in mechanical failure.

facts.headline: Murray Walker hired to lead ITV's F1 coverage
facts.detail: Veteran commentator Murray Walker was announced as the lead voice of ITV's new Formula 1 broadcast deal.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi edges Cevert at the 1973 Argentine Grand Prix
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi passed Tyrrell's Francois Cevert in the closing laps to win the season opener; Cevert died in practice for the season finale that same year.

facts.headline: Takuma Sato is born
facts.detail: Takuma Sato, later a fan-favourite for his aggressive overtakes and a two-time Indy 500 winner, was born in Tokyo.

facts.headline: Alain Prost's F1 team is liquidated
facts.detail: A French court ordered Alain Prost's namesake team into liquidation over $30 million in debts, making it F1's first major team casualty in seven years.

facts.headline: Jody Scheckter is born
facts.detail: 1979 World Champion Jody Scheckter was born in East London, South Africa; Francois Cevert's death in 1973 changed him from a reckless driver into a cautious one.

facts.headline: Reutemann wins the 1978 Brazilian Grand Prix on Michelin tyres
facts.detail: Carlos Reutemann's win for Ferrari ended Goodyear's dominance and gave Michelin its first F1 victory.

facts.headline: Rudolf Caracciola is born
facts.detail: Rudolf Caracciola, a three-time European Champion for Mercedes in the 1930s, was born in Remagen, Germany.

facts.headline: McLaren co-founder Teddy Mayer dies
facts.detail: Teddy Mayer, who helped establish McLaren in 1963 and led the team through title wins with Fittipaldi and Hunt in the 1970s, died at 73.

facts.headline: Jo Bonnier is born
facts.detail: Jo Bonnier won once from 109 F1 starts, at the 1959 Dutch Grand Prix, before dying in a crash at Le Mans in 1972.

facts.headline: FIA introduces flight-recorder black boxes
facts.detail: Following Ayrton Senna's death in 1994, the FIA mandated aviation-style black boxes in F1 cars as part of a wider safety overhaul.

facts.headline: Narain Karthikeyan signs with Jordan
facts.detail: Narain Karthikeyan signed with Jordan, becoming the first Indian driver in Formula 1.

facts.headline: Lewis Hamilton announces his move to Ferrari
facts.detail: Hamilton announced he would leave Mercedes for Ferrari in 2025, ending an 11-year partnership that brought six world titles.

facts.headline: Valentino Rossi impresses in an F1 test with Ferrari
facts.detail: MotoGP star Valentino Rossi set the ninth-fastest time on his first full day testing for Ferrari, finishing within a second of Michael Schumacher.

facts.headline: Roger Williamson is born
facts.detail: British driver Roger Williamson was born; he died at Zandvoort in only his second F1 race in 1973 after a crash and fire, despite David Purley's rescue attempt.

facts.headline: Renault turbo pioneer Jean-Pierre Jabouille dies
facts.detail: Jean-Pierre Jabouille, who won two races during Renault's pioneering turbo era, died at 80.

facts.headline: Tony Gaze is born, later the first Australian F1 driver
facts.detail: Tony Gaze, born in Melbourne, became the first Australian to compete in a Grand Prix; he was also a decorated WWII Spitfire pilot who helped found the Goodwood circuit.

facts.headline: Daimler acquires a 40% stake in McLaren
facts.detail: Mercedes' parent company Daimler bought 40% of McLaren, deepening a partnership that eventually led to Mercedes launching its own F1 team in 2010.

facts.headline: First Russian-flagged F1 car is introduced
facts.detail: Midland F1 Racing unveiled the M16, the first Formula 1 car to race under the Russian flag, after Alex Shnaider's takeover of the former Jordan team.

facts.headline: Jacques Laffite wins back-to-back at the 1979 Brazilian GP
facts.detail: Laffite took his second consecutive win for Ligier, with teammate Patrick Depailler second.

facts.headline: Nick Heidfeld drives an F1 car across a frozen lake
facts.detail: For a promotional event in St. Moritz, Heidfeld drove a spiked-tyre BMW Sauber across a frozen lake, with the engine warmed every 30 minutes to stop it freezing.

facts.headline: Michael Schumacher founds karting team KSM
facts.detail: Schumacher launched the KSM karting team in Germany's national championship, saying he owed everything to karting.

facts.headline: Fernando Alonso's F1 debut with Minardi is announced
facts.detail: Flavio Briatore announced Alonso's move to Minardi for 2001; he would go on to win back-to-back titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006.

facts.headline: Last surviving Silver Arrows driver dies
facts.detail: Manfred von Brauchitsch, who won three races for Mercedes in the 1930s including setting a lap record at Monaco that stood 18 years, died at 97.

facts.headline: FOCA stages a breakaway race at Kyalami
facts.detail: Amid a power struggle with governing body FISA, the Formula One Constructors' Association ran an unsanctioned race at Kyalami, forcing a compromise that led to the first Concorde Agreement.

facts.headline: Robert Kubica is badly injured in a rally crash
facts.detail: Kubica suffered severe arm, leg, and hand fractures in a rally crash in Italy, ending his F1 career for years; he returned with Williams in 2019.

facts.headline: Last survivor of the first-ever F1 race dies
facts.detail: Tony Rolt, the final surviving competitor from the 1950 British Grand Prix, died at 89; he'd also won Le Mans in 1953 and escaped Colditz Castle by glider as a WWII POW.

facts.headline: 1981 South African GP run as a non-championship race
facts.detail: The FISA-FOCA feud forced the race to run outside the championship as a Formula Libre event; Carlos Reutemann won for Williams.

facts.headline: Pierre Gasly is born
facts.detail: Pierre Gasly, who later won the 2020 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso, was born in Rouen, France.

facts.headline: Force India unveils its first car
facts.detail: Force India launched the VJM01 in Mumbai under Vijay Mallya, though it scored no points in its debut season.

facts.headline: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Corporation is formed
facts.detail: The organisation set up to manage the Indianapolis Speedway paved the crumbling original track surface with bricks, giving it the nickname 'The Brickyard'.

facts.headline: Michael Schumacher tests the title-winning Ferrari F2000
facts.detail: Schumacher shook down the F2000 at Fiorano; the car went on to win nine races and deliver Ferrari's first drivers' title in 21 years.

facts.headline: Gerhard Berger buys 50% of Toro Rosso
facts.detail: Former driver Gerhard Berger acquired a half-share in Toro Rosso from Red Bull's Dietrich Mateschitz, in a deal that included Mateschitz buying into Berger's shipping company.

facts.headline: Ayrton Senna is left without an F1 seat
facts.detail: Ron Dennis named Mika Hakkinen and Michael Andretti as McLaren's 1993 drivers, leaving three-time champion Ayrton Senna without a contract; he returned to McLaren for the opener regardless.

facts.headline: Max Mosley warns F1 is too reliant on manufacturers
facts.detail: FIA president Max Mosley cautioned that Formula 1 needed to support independent teams more; by 2009 BMW, Ford, Honda, and Toyota had all quit the sport, proving him right.

facts.headline: John Surtees is born
facts.detail: John Surtees, the only person in history to win world championships on both two wheels and four, was born in Surrey; he won 500cc motorcycle titles before taking the 1964 F1 title with Ferrari.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi wins the first championship Brazilian Grand Prix
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi triumphed in front of his home crowd at Interlagos, beating Jackie Stewart and Denny Hulme as Brazil's race joined the world championship for the first time.

facts.headline: Liam Lawson is born
facts.detail: Liam Lawson, who made his F1 debut for AlphaTauri in 2023 and later partnered Max Verstappen at Red Bull, was born in New Zealand.

facts.headline: Renault co-founder Louis Renault is born
facts.detail: Louis Renault, who co-founded the Renault company in Paris, was born; his legacy is complicated by his wartime collaboration with Germany, and he died in 1944 awaiting trial.

facts.headline: Peter 'Bono' Bonnington is born
facts.detail: Peter Bonnington, who became Lewis Hamilton's race engineer at Mercedes through his 2012-2024 title-winning run, was born in Britain.

facts.headline: Sandstorms halt F1 testing in Bahrain
facts.detail: Ferrari, BMW Sauber, and Toyota chose Bahrain to avoid rain during testing, only for a sandstorm to stop the session after just one lap each.

facts.headline: Alain Prost buys Ligier to found Prost Grand Prix
facts.detail: Four-time champion Alain Prost took over the Ligier team to create Prost Grand Prix, which scored two podiums in its debut season before folding in 2001.

facts.headline: Last driver to race a Bugatti in F1 dies
facts.detail: Maurice Trintignant, who drove a Bugatti Type 251 at the 1956 French GP and won Monaco twice, died at 87.

facts.headline: Ronnie Peterson is born
facts.detail: Swedish fan-favourite Ronnie Peterson was born; he died from complications after a crash at the 1978 Italian Grand Prix, just as he was set to lead McLaren the following year.

facts.headline: McLaren launches its silver 1997 car with the Spice Girls in attendance
facts.detail: McLaren unveiled its first silver livery at a lavish launch event; the car won its debut race, the team's first victory since Senna in 1993.

facts.headline: FIA bans refuelling before qualifying
facts.detail: Max Mosley's FIA ruled that cars must qualify on race fuel, forcing new strategic trade-offs between grid position and race pace until refuelling itself was banned in 2010.

facts.headline: Graham Hill is born
facts.detail: Two-time champion Graham Hill, the only driver ever to complete motorsport's Triple Crown (F1 title, Indy 500, and Le Mans), was born in London; he died in a 1975 plane crash.

facts.headline: George Russell is born
facts.detail: George Russell, who won back-to-back GP3 and F2 titles before joining Williams in 2019 and Mercedes in 2022, was born in Britain.

facts.headline: Jean Behra is born
facts.detail: Fearless French driver Jean Behra survived 12 major crashes and lost an ear in one, before dying at Avus in 1959 driving a Porsche.

facts.headline: Jenson Button survives a 160mph bird strike
facts.detail: During Williams testing at Kyalami, a bird struck the airbox directly above Button's head; he was unhurt and drove back to the pits.

facts.headline: F1 teams vote to legalise traction control
facts.detail: Traction control, banned since 1994 but suspected of covert use, was officially permitted until being banned again in 2008 with a standard ECU.

facts.headline: The first event ever called a 'Grand Prix' is held
facts.detail: The inaugural Grand Prix took place at Pau, France, won by Maurice Farman; the term wasn't used again until 1906.

facts.headline: 15-year-old Lewis Hamilton declares his F1 ambition
facts.detail: Inspired by Jenson Button's Williams seat, Hamilton told the press he wanted to beat Button to become the youngest F1 driver ever; he joined McLaren in 2007 and became champion in 2008.

facts.headline: Ecclestone proposes a Las Vegas Grand Prix
facts.detail: After tensions with Indianapolis following the 2005 US GP tyre fiasco, Bernie Ecclestone floated Las Vegas as a new host; the city didn't return to the calendar until 2023.

facts.headline: Enzo Ferrari is born
facts.detail: Enzo Ferrari, founder of the only team to compete in every F1 season since 1950, was born in Modena; under his leadership Scuderia Ferrari won 9 drivers' and 8 constructors' titles.

facts.headline: FIA mandates black-box flight recorders for 1998
facts.detail: Following Senna's death, FIA president Max Mosley announced all F1 cars would carry accident data recorders from the new season.

facts.headline: Lewis Hamilton wins a Laureus World Sports Award
facts.detail: Hamilton was honoured after narrowly missing the 2007 title by one point in his rookie season, tying teammate Fernando Alonso's score.

facts.headline: First F1 car driven in the Middle East
facts.detail: Neel Jani drove a Sauber through the streets of Manama, Bahrain, promoting that year's inaugural Bahrain Grand Prix.

facts.headline: Ecclestone criticises the switch to V8 engines
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone called the hasty decision to replace 3.0-litre V10s with 2.4-litre V8s 'total nonsense,' saying teams hadn't grasped the development costs.

facts.headline: Jacques Villeneuve releases a music album
facts.detail: Villeneuve launched his debut record 'Private Paradise,' writing six of its 13 tracks, including one for his father Gilles.

facts.headline: Roger Penske is born
facts.detail: Roger Penske, whose team won its sole F1 race with John Watson at the 1976 Austrian GP, went on to dominate American IndyCar and sports car racing.

facts.headline: Williams trio go on trial over Senna's death
facts.detail: Frank Williams, Patrick Head, and Adrian Newey stood trial in Italy for culpable homicide over Ayrton Senna's 1994 death; all were acquitted after a year-long trial.

facts.headline: Briatore defends Raikkonen's nightclub visit
facts.detail: Renault boss Flavio Briatore called Kimi Raikkonen a 'breath of fresh air' after criticism of his visit to a London lap-dancing club, saying drivers shouldn't be robots.

facts.headline: Peter Gethin is born
facts.detail: Peter Gethin won the closest finish in F1 history at the 1971 Italian GP, beating Ronnie Peterson by just 0.01 seconds with five cars covered by under a second.

facts.headline: Winner of the first-ever Grand Prix dies
facts.detail: Ferenc Szisz, who won the inaugural 1906 French Grand Prix at Le Mans for Renault, died in France at 70.

facts.headline: Mosley says Senna should have been disqualified in 1990
facts.detail: FIA president Max Mosley said Ayrton Senna's deliberate collision with Alain Prost at Suzuka, which won him the title, was dangerous enough to warrant exclusion.

facts.headline: Niki Lauda is born
facts.detail: Three-time champion Niki Lauda was born in Austria; he returned from near-fatal burns in the 1976 Nurburgring crash to race again just weeks later.

facts.headline: Andrea Stella is born
facts.detail: Andrea Stella, who became McLaren's team principal and led them to the 2024 and 2025 Constructors' titles, was born in Italy.

facts.headline: Ferrari renews its Marlboro sponsorship
facts.detail: Ferrari extended its tobacco sponsorship deal with Philip Morris, reportedly worth $1 billion over seven years, despite looming EU advertising bans.

facts.headline: Fangio is kidnapped by Cuban revolutionaries
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio was abducted at gunpoint by Castro-linked rebels before the 1958 Havana GP; he was held safely and released unharmed after the race.

facts.headline: Satoru Nakajima is born
facts.detail: Satoru Nakajima became Japan's first full-time F1 driver, racing for Lotus and Tyrrell from 1987-1991; his son Kazuki later drove for Williams.

facts.headline: Hans Herrmann is born
facts.detail: Hans Herrmann raced F1 across four separate stints in the 1950s and 60s before winning Porsche's first overall Le Mans victory in 1970.

facts.headline: Alain Prost is born
facts.detail: Four-time champion Alain Prost was born in France; his 51 wins and fierce rivalry with Ayrton Senna defined a generation of F1.

facts.headline: Senna crash report points to steering failure
facts.detail: A 500-page Italian investigation into Ayrton Senna's fatal 1994 Imola crash suggested a steering column failure, though the cause remained disputed and all Williams staff were later acquitted.

facts.headline: Karthikeyan told to change his flag-themed helmet
facts.detail: The Indian government initially ordered Narain Karthikeyan to remove the Indian flag from his helmet over flag code rules, before reversing the decision ahead of his F1 debut.

facts.headline: Tony Brooks, the 'Racing Dentist', is born
facts.detail: Tony Brooks balanced F1 racing with dental training, winning six races for Vanwall and Ferrari; he was the last surviving 1950s Grand Prix winner until his death in 2022.

facts.headline: Francois Cevert is born
facts.detail: French driver Francois Cevert won once for Tyrrell alongside Jackie Stewart before dying in a practice crash at the 1973 US Grand Prix.

facts.headline: Jean Todt is born
facts.detail: Jean Todt led Ferrari to five consecutive titles with Michael Schumacher as team principal, then served as FIA president from 2009 to 2021.

facts.headline: Jean-Pierre Wimille is born
facts.detail: A French Resistance hero and dominant post-war racer, Wimille won four Grands Prix in 1947-48 before dying in a practice crash for the 1949 Argentine GP.

facts.headline: Robert La Caze, F1's only Moroccan-flagged driver, is born
facts.detail: La Caze raced the 1958 Moroccan GP as a privateer and later became the oldest living World Championship driver before his death in 2015.

facts.headline: Honda unveils its 'Earth Dreams' environmental livery
facts.detail: Honda's RA107 swapped sponsor logos for a world map to promote environmental awareness; the car underperformed and Honda left F1 by 2009.

facts.headline: Peter Revson is born
facts.detail: Revlon heir Peter Revson won the 1973 British and Canadian GPs for McLaren before dying in a 1974 testing crash ahead of the South African GP.

facts.headline: A hill-climb race is held inside a six-story Paris building
facts.detail: Robert Benoist organised a non-timed 'hill-climb' up interior ramps of a new Paris garage, with 15 drivers taking part to launch the venue.

facts.headline: Mark Webber drives a Williams F1 car over Sydney Harbour Bridge
facts.detail: Webber closed the iconic bridge for two hours to power his 900bhp FW26 across it, kicking off the Australian racing season.

facts.headline: Mario Andretti is born
facts.detail: Mario Andretti won the 1978 F1 title with Lotus and remains one of the only drivers to win the Indy 500, Daytona 500, and an F1 championship.

facts.headline: Surer and Prost crash in dramatic SA GP qualifying
facts.detail: Marc Surer was trapped for 30 minutes after hitting a wall, while Alain Prost escaped two scares; a heated meeting over the 1981 skirts ban followed, with Jones and Watson reportedly resigning in protest.

facts.headline: Minardi barely gets its car to the grid
facts.detail: Paul Stoddart's underfunded Minardi launched its car just before the season; when Fernando Alonso finished 12th in the opener, Stoddart likened it to winning the title.

facts.headline: Masten Gregory, 'The Kansas City Flash', is born
facts.detail: American driver Masten Gregory raced F1 from 1957-1965 and won the 1965 Le Mans 24 Hours in a Ferrari 250LM alongside Jochen Rindt.

facts.headline: Bahrain GP practice runs on a leap day
facts.detail: On this rare calendar date, Daniel Ricciardo topped FP1 for RB and Lewis Hamilton led FP2 for Mercedes at the 2024 season opener.

facts.headline: Jackie Stewart wins the 1969 season opener
facts.detail: Stewart won the South African GP for Matra from fourth on the grid, with Graham Hill second for Lotus.

facts.headline: Jody Scheckter becomes the first South African to win his home GP
facts.detail: Scheckter took the lead from Carlos Pace on lap three and held on to win the 1975 South African GP for Tyrrell.

facts.headline: Ron Dennis steps down as McLaren chairman
facts.detail: Dennis, who joined McLaren in 1980 and guided the team to 17 world titles, left the CEO role after a shareholder meeting.

facts.headline: Schumacher survives a terrifying 175mph crash
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Ferrari flipped twice after losing control at Melbourne's Turn 6 during Australian GP practice.

facts.headline: Ecclestone dismisses women's chances in F1
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone said women would likely never get the opportunity to race in F1 because no team would take the risk.

facts.headline: Bahrain GP moves to Saturday for Ramadan
facts.detail: F1 shifted the race day for the first time to avoid clashing with Ramadan observance later in the season.

facts.headline: John Parry-Thomas becomes the first land speed record fatality
facts.detail: The Welsh driver died when a drive chain broke on his car 'Babs' at 170mph during a land speed record attempt.

facts.headline: Lella Lombardi dies
facts.detail: Lombardi remains the only woman to score a Formula 1 point, finishing sixth at the 1975 Spanish GP.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins a chaotic season-opening Melbourne GP
facts.detail: Two safety cars and a high retirement rate marked the 2002 Australian GP, which Schumacher won for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Jim Clark is born
facts.detail: Clark and Colin Chapman formed one of F1's great partnerships at Lotus, winning world titles in 1963 and 1965.

facts.headline: A marshal is killed at the Australian GP
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve's car collided with Ralf Schumacher and flew into a wall, and a detached wheel fatally struck a trackside marshal.

facts.headline: F1 holds its 300th World Championship Grand Prix
facts.detail: The milestone South African GP came 28 years after the championship began in 1950.

facts.headline: Ross Brawn buys Honda's F1 team, forming Brawn GP
facts.detail: Brawn acquired the team after Honda withdrew from F1 amid the global financial crisis; Brawn GP won the title that year.

facts.headline: Lauda wins in South Africa on his way back to the title
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's Ferrari victory was a key step in reclaiming the championship from James Hunt.

facts.headline: Verstappen sweeps pole and victory to open 2023
facts.detail: Max Verstappen won the Bahrain GP season opener with teammate Sergio Perez close behind.

facts.headline: Mario Andretti wins his first F1 race
facts.detail: Andretti took his maiden Grand Prix victory at the South African GP for Ferrari, beating Jackie Stewart by nearly 21 seconds.

facts.headline: Lauda wins his third straight race
facts.detail: Niki Lauda beat rival James Hunt by 1.3 seconds at the South African GP in his Ferrari 312T.

facts.headline: Fisichella wins the season opener from pole
facts.detail: Giancarlo Fisichella won the Australian GP for Renault ahead of Rubens Barrichello's Ferrari.

facts.headline: Eddie Irvine wins his first race for Ferrari
facts.detail: Irvine capitalized on McLaren trouble to win the Australian GP, starting ahead of teammate Schumacher.

facts.headline: Schumacher opens a dominant 2004 season with a win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Melbourne victory signaled the start of Ferrari's most dominant year.

facts.headline: Verstappen crashes out in Q1 as Mercedes locks the front row
facts.detail: George Russell took a stunning pole for the season-opening Australian GP after Verstappen lost the rear of his Red Bull.

facts.headline: Coulthard lets Hakkinen through to win in Australia
facts.detail: David Coulthard deliberately slowed to hand teammate Mika Hakkinen a controversial McLaren victory.

facts.headline: F1 introduces a two-part qualifying format
facts.detail: Ecclestone's new format split qualifying across Saturday and Sunday to boost exposure for smaller teams.

facts.headline: Russell converts pole into a Mercedes 1-2
facts.detail: George Russell won the season-opening Australian GP ahead of teammate Kimi Antonelli, with Leclerc third.

facts.headline: Coulthard ends McLaren's 50-race winless streak
facts.detail: David Coulthard won the Australian GP from fourth on the grid, also marking Mercedes' first F1 win since Fangio.

facts.headline: Coulthard wins the season opener again
facts.detail: David Coulthard took victory at the Australian GP for McLaren, with Juan Pablo Montoya second for Williams.

facts.headline: Ecclestone rules out F1's return to Africa
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone cited the continent's football World Cup commitments as a major distraction from hosting F1.

facts.headline: John Surtees dies
facts.detail: Surtees remains the only person to win World Championships on both two wheels and four, in motorcycle racing and F1.

facts.headline: Senna wins with a car he'd had for just ten days
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna took his 27th career win at the season-opening US GP in Phoenix, in a McLaren he'd barely tested.

facts.headline: Damon Hill wins Australia's first season-opening race
facts.detail: Hill led home a Williams victory as Australia hosted the opening round for the first time.

facts.headline: Jenson Button survives a 160mph practice crash on his F1 weekend debut
facts.detail: The future 2009 champion badly damaged his Williams FW22 at the Australian GP but was fifth-fastest before the crash.

facts.headline: Senna wins the 1990 season opener in Phoenix
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna took victory in his McLaren-Honda despite a rain-disrupted qualifying session.

facts.headline: Arturo Merzario is born
facts.detail: Merzario raced 57 Grands Prix but is best remembered for heroically pulling Niki Lauda from his burning car at the 1976 German GP.

facts.headline: Ferrari offers Schumacher a record-breaking deal to stay
facts.detail: Ferrari proposed a reported £52 million contract to keep Michael Schumacher amid rumors of a rival move.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins the season opener for Ferrari
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher won the Australian GP with teammate Rubens Barrichello second.

facts.headline: F1 debuts three-stage knockout qualifying
facts.detail: The new format split qualifying into three knockout stages at the season-opening Bahrain GP.

facts.headline: Murray Walker dies
facts.detail: The legendary voice of F1 broadcasting left behind a five-decade commentary legacy renowned for its passion and energy.

facts.headline: Keke Rosberg is disqualified from a Brazilian GP for the second year running
facts.detail: Rosberg suffered the same fate in 1983 that had denied him a podium the year before.

facts.headline: The Bahrain GP is postponed due to civil unrest
facts.detail: The race, originally set for this day, had been postponed weeks earlier as unrest erupted across Bahrain.

facts.headline: Charlie Whiting dies
facts.detail: The much-loved F1 Race Director, who rose from Brabham chief mechanic to the FIA's top official, died suddenly ahead of the season.

facts.headline: Prost dominates the final South African GP at Kyalami
facts.detail: Alain Prost's Williams won despite a challenging start, outpacing Senna, Hill, and the field.

facts.headline: Antonelli becomes the youngest pole sitter in F1 history
facts.detail: Kimi Antonelli stormed to a stunning Chinese GP pole at 19, breaking the record with a blistering lap.

facts.headline: The Australian GP is cancelled hours before practice
facts.detail: The COVID-19 pandemic forced F1 to scrap the 2020 season opener at the last minute.

facts.headline: Antonelli converts his record pole into a maiden win
facts.detail: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest-ever F1 winner, finishing ahead of teammate George Russell at the Chinese GP.

facts.headline: Alan Jones wins at Long Beach
facts.detail: Jones took victory and fastest lap in his Williams at the US GP West, with Riccardo Patrese scoring Arrows' first pole.

facts.headline: F1 enters the turbo-hybrid V6 era
facts.detail: The 1.6-litre turbocharged V6 made its debut, the first F1 turbo engines since 1988; Nico Rosberg won for Mercedes.

facts.headline: Renault re-enters F1 by buying Benetton
facts.detail: Renault paid $110 million to reacquire the Benetton team, installing Flavio Briatore as team principal.

facts.headline: Eddie Irvine's dig at Damon Hill backfires
facts.detail: Irvine criticized Hill's Australian GP win, but Hill went on to claim the 1996 Drivers' Championship.

facts.headline: A Blair-Ecclestone donation scandal rocks UK politics
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone's £1 million donation to Tony Blair's Labour Party was returned amid claims it bought F1 a tobacco-ad exemption.

facts.headline: Schumacher takes Ferrari's 150th pole position
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Malaysian GP pole came during a weekend marred by an early Montoya collision.

facts.headline: Albert Park's long-used layout runs for the last time
facts.detail: The 2019 Australian GP was the final race on the circuit configuration used since 1996.

facts.headline: Carlos Pace dies in a plane crash
facts.detail: The beloved Brazilian driver, for whom Interlagos is now named, died at 32 near Sao Paulo.

facts.headline: Lewis Hamilton podiums on his F1 debut
facts.detail: Hamilton finished third for McLaren at the season-opening Australian GP, which Kimi Raikkonen won for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Jean Todt resigns as Ferrari CEO
facts.detail: Todt stepped down after leading Ferrari through its Schumacher-era dominance, later becoming FIA president.

facts.headline: Tony Blair admits breaking disclosure rules over an Ecclestone gift
facts.detail: Blair had failed to declare a £1,500 hospitality gift from Bernie Ecclestone tied to the tobacco-ad controversy.

facts.headline: Fisichella leads start to finish in Malaysia
facts.detail: Giancarlo Fisichella held off teammate Fernando Alonso for his first win in a year.

facts.headline: Perez claims pole and victory in Saudi Arabia
facts.detail: Sergio Perez won ahead of Red Bull teammate Verstappen, with Fernando Alonso completing the podium.

facts.headline: Eddie Jordan dies
facts.detail: The founder of the Jordan Grand Prix team passed away after a battle with cancer.

facts.headline: Leclerc wins his first race since 2019
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc dominated the Bahrain GP from pole, leading all but two laps.

facts.headline: Hamilton claims his 50th career pole
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton started from pole at the Australian GP, though teammate Nico Rosberg won the race.

facts.headline: Ayrton Senna is born
facts.detail: Senna won three World Drivers' Championships (1988, 1990, 1991) and 41 Grands Prix in one of F1's most storied careers.

facts.headline: Piquet and Rosberg are disqualified for underweight cars
facts.detail: The pair had finished first and second at the Brazilian GP before being stripped of the result.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins in Malaysia as Button scores a milestone podium
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Ferrari won from pole as future champion Jenson Button also impressed.

facts.headline: Peter Revson dies practicing at Kyalami
facts.detail: The American driver, 35, lost his life when his Shadow crashed during a practice session in South Africa.

facts.headline: Mick Schumacher is born
facts.detail: The son of seven-time champion Michael Schumacher later raced in F1 himself for Haas.

facts.headline: Colin McRae flirts with an F1 switch
facts.detail: The World Rally Champion revealed he'd tested with Jackie Stewart's Stewart Grand Prix team.

facts.headline: Alonso takes his first F1 pole and podium
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso qualified on pole and finished third at the Malaysian GP for Renault.

facts.headline: Jaime Alguersuari is born, later F1's youngest-ever driver
facts.detail: Alguersuari broke the youngest-driver record at 19 when he debuted for Toro Rosso in 2009.

facts.headline: Piastri wins his maiden Grand Prix in a McLaren 1-2
facts.detail: Oscar Piastri converted his first pole into a dominant win at the Chinese GP, leading McLaren home in front.

facts.headline: Senna wins despite crippling cramps
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna won in Brazil while stuck in sixth gear after losing two gears, needing help to exit his car afterward.

facts.headline: Vettel wins amid Multi-21 fallout
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel took victory in Malaysia days after defying team orders to pass Mark Webber, who nearly boycotted the podium.

facts.headline: Webber doubts Schumacher's F1 comeback
facts.detail: Mark Webber said he'd never seen a truly phenomenal comeback, ahead of Schumacher's return after four years away.

facts.headline: Ayrton Senna makes his F1 debut
facts.detail: Senna's Toleman retired after eight laps of his home Brazilian GP with a turbo failure; Martin Brundle also debuted that day.

facts.headline: Vettel marks his 100th podium with a win
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel's Australian GP victory also brought up his 48th career win.

facts.headline: A rebuilt Interlagos hosts F1 again after a decade
facts.detail: Alain Prost won for Ferrari as Brazil's home race returned to a reconstructed Interlagos circuit.

facts.headline: Mansell wins on his Ferrari debut with F1's first semi-automatic gearbox
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's unexpected Brazilian GP victory introduced a technology that would reshape the sport.

facts.headline: Schumacher and Coulthard are disqualified hours after finishing 1-2
facts.detail: Fuel irregularities stripped both drivers of their Brazilian GP result, promoting Gerhard Berger to the win.

facts.headline: Lella Lombardi is born
facts.detail: Lombardi remains the only woman to score a point in Formula 1 World Championship history.

facts.headline: Watson wins from 22nd on the grid
facts.detail: John Watson's US GP West victory from the back of the field remains F1's record furthest starting position for a win.

facts.headline: Jean-Marie Balestre dies
facts.detail: The authoritarian former FIA president, who led the federation from 1985 to 1993, left a lasting mark on F1.

facts.headline: David Coulthard is born
facts.detail: Coulthard went on to win 13 Grands Prix and remains a familiar face in F1 media.

facts.headline: F1 introduces the safety car
facts.detail: Persistent rain and debris at the Brazilian GP prompted the first-ever use of a safety car in the sport.

facts.headline: F1 races at Long Beach for the first time
facts.detail: The inaugural United States GP West kicked off what became a beloved southern California street race.

facts.headline: Verstappen dominates practice ahead of the 2021 opener
facts.detail: Max Verstappen topped all three practice sessions before qualifying on pole for the Bahrain GP.

facts.headline: Hakkinen and McLaren complete a hat-trick of dominance
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen's third straight win came with McLaren's third consecutive 1-2 finish, leading from pole with the fastest lap.

facts.headline: F1 shifts Brazil's race from Interlagos to Jacarepagua
facts.detail: Safety concerns over Sao Paulo's expanding slums pushed the Brazilian GP to Rio de Janeiro.

facts.headline: Antonelli takes the championship lead with a Suzuka win
facts.detail: Kimi Antonelli's defining Japanese GP victory moved him into the lead of the 2026 title race.

facts.headline: Reutemann becomes the first Argentinian winner since Fangio
facts.detail: Carlos Reutemann's Brabham won at Kyalami, 16 years after Juan Manuel Fangio's last Argentinian victory.

facts.headline: Lucien Bianchi dies testing at Le Mans
facts.detail: The Belgian driver's Alfa Romeo crashed into a telegraph pole during a test session.

facts.headline: Hamilton ties Jim Clark's British pole record
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's 33rd career pole in Malaysia matched Clark's long-standing mark for a British driver.

facts.headline: Damon Hill breaks his father's win record
facts.detail: Hill's 15th F1 victory at the Brazilian GP surpassed Graham Hill's career win tally.

facts.headline: Pele waves the checkered flag in Brazil
facts.detail: The football legend took part in the ceremonial duties at the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Hamilton wins as F1 debuts a new DRS zone
facts.detail: An extra DRS zone between turns 3 and 4 aimed to boost overtaking at the Bahrain GP, which Hamilton won.

facts.headline: Irvine wins a libel case over a doctored photo
facts.detail: Eddie Irvine was awarded £25,000 after Talksport altered a photo of him to make it look like he was endorsing the station.

facts.headline: Barrichello's home race ends on lap two
facts.detail: The Brazilian's race was cut short after colliding with Ralf Schumacher at his home Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Jack Brabham is born
facts.detail: A three-time champion who later won a title in his own car, Brabham was the last surviving 1950s World Champion at his death in 2014.

facts.headline: Reutemann wins Long Beach after Villeneuve's late crash
facts.detail: Carlos Reutemann inherited the lead from his crashing Ferrari teammate Gilles Villeneuve, beating Mario Andretti's Lotus by 11 seconds.

facts.headline: Verstappen wins as three champions share the Australian GP podium
facts.detail: Max Verstappen led home Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso in a record-setting podium of three world champions.

facts.headline: Andretti becomes the first American to win an F1 race on home soil
facts.detail: Mario Andretti's Lotus 78 triumphed at Long Beach, heralding F1's ground-effect era.

facts.headline: McLaren signs a 13-year-old Lewis Hamilton
facts.detail: Ron Dennis brought the karting prodigy into McLaren's Young Driver Program, nine years before his F1 debut.

facts.headline: Piquet's pre-race insults overshadow the 1988 season opener
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet publicly insulted Ayrton Senna, Nigel Mansell, and their families before the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Lauda wins his comeback race
facts.detail: Niki Lauda took his first win in nearly five years at Long Beach, just his third race back from a self-imposed two-year retirement.

facts.headline: F1 races in the Middle East for the first time
facts.detail: The inaugural Bahrain GP saw Michael Schumacher dominate from start to finish for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Vettel and Webber give Red Bull a Malaysian 1-2
facts.detail: Vettel led home Webber, who'd claimed a dramatic rain-soaked pole position.

facts.headline: Button wins again as Brawn GP's fairytale start continues
facts.detail: Jenson Button took the second of six consecutive season-opening wins for the newly formed Brawn GP, in a torrential Malaysian downpour.

facts.headline: F1's first-ever Vietnamese GP is cancelled before it happens
facts.detail: The planned Hanoi street race, set for this day, was postponed and then scrapped amid COVID-19 and the arrest of a local political figure.

facts.headline: F1's haves and have-nots collide in Brazil
facts.detail: McLaren arrived with six cars for its drivers while the struggling Andrea Moda team fought just to field two.

facts.headline: F1's 700th championship race ends up decided in Paris
facts.detail: One of the sport's most controversial results was ultimately settled at FIA headquarters after the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Oscar Piastri is born
facts.detail: Piastri rose through karting and junior categories to become one of F1's brightest young talents.

facts.headline: F1 holds its first-ever night race in Bahrain
facts.detail: The 900th World Championship race saw Lewis Hamilton win under Sakhir's floodlights for Mercedes.

facts.headline: Jim Clark dies in a Formula Two crash
facts.detail: The double world champion's death at Hockenheim, in what should have been a minor race, sent shockwaves through motorsport.

facts.headline: Ghinzani's car is torn in half in a horrific crash
facts.detail: The Osella driver's monocoque cartwheeled down the track and burst into flames at the South African GP, but he survived.

facts.headline: McLaren is charged over the 'Liegate' scandal
facts.detail: The FIA pursued McLaren for bringing the sport into disrepute after Lewis Hamilton misled stewards at the Australian GP.

facts.headline: Villeneuve wins a chaotic Long Beach race
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve led from the start at the disorganized US GP West, which began amid a chaotic multi-car grid.

facts.headline: McLaren locks out the podium's top two in Malaysia
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso won ahead of teammate Lewis Hamilton, overtaking pole-sitter Felipe Massa's Ferrari.

facts.headline: Vettel beats Hamilton in a tight title battle race
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel, defending a seven-point championship lead, won the Bahrain GP over his closest rival.

facts.headline: Jacques Villeneuve is born
facts.detail: The son of Gilles Villeneuve won the 1997 World Championship after first making his name in IndyCar.

facts.headline: The Argentine GP returns after 14 years away
facts.detail: Damon Hill won its long-awaited comeback race after pole-sitter and teammate David Coulthard retired.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins his third straight race to open the season
facts.detail: A well-executed pit strategy handed Michael Schumacher a perfect start to the 2000 championship.

facts.headline: Mike Hawthorn is born
facts.detail: The charismatic, bow-tie-wearing racer became Britain's first-ever Formula One World Champion.

facts.headline: The Australian GP returns after a three-year absence
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc dominated the long-awaited comeback race for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Vettel leads pole to flag for his second win in a row
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel controlled the Malaysian GP for Red Bull, with Jenson Button second for McLaren.

facts.headline: Senna wins his 38th race in treacherous conditions
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's European GP victory came in ever-changing weather that Damon Hill called a nightmare.

facts.headline: Hakkinen wins his tenth Grand Prix
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen beat Michael Schumacher's Ferrari by 4.9 seconds at the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Stirling Moss dies
facts.detail: Widely praised as the greatest all-round racing driver never to win the World Championship, Moss became a professional driver in 1948.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins amid controversy after colliding with Coulthard
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Argentine GP victory was overshadowed by a fifth-lap clash while attempting an overtake.

facts.headline: Prost wins in scorching heat for his third victory at the same race
facts.detail: Alain Prost fought through the field from fifth on the grid to win the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: Senna beats Mansell by 0.014 seconds
facts.detail: Senna's Lotus edged Mansell's Williams in a drag race to the line at the Spanish GP, one of F1's closest-ever finishes.

facts.headline: Villeneuve wins the 600th championship Grand Prix while battling illness
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve fought through a stomach bug to narrowly beat Eddie Irvine's Ferrari in Argentina.

facts.headline: Max Mosley is born
facts.detail: Mosley co-founded March Engineering before becoming FIA president and one of the most influential regulators in F1 history.

facts.headline: The first-ever Monaco Grand Prix is won by a British driver
facts.detail: William Grover-Williams' Bugatti beat the favored Mercedes contenders around the streets of Monte Carlo.

facts.headline: Schumacher sets a Ferrari record with his 97th race for the team
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's dominant San Marino win extended his championship lead to 14 points.

facts.headline: F1 holds its 1000th World Championship race
facts.detail: The milestone Chinese GP came 69 years after the series began at Silverstone in 1950.

facts.headline: Harvey Postlethwaite dies
facts.detail: One of British motorsport's most distinguished engineers, Postlethwaite served as technical director at Hesketh, Ferrari, Tyrrell, and Sauber.

facts.headline: The Schumacher brothers finish first and second
facts.detail: Ralf Schumacher won the San Marino GP ahead of older brother Michael, the first siblings to finish 1-2 in F1 history.

facts.headline: Rosberg wins his first race, and Mercedes' first since returning as a works team
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg's dominant Chinese GP victory was a landmark for both driver and team.

facts.headline: Frank Williams is born
facts.detail: The founder of the Williams F1 team became one of the sport's most respected and enduring figures.

facts.headline: Ron Dennis's departure as McLaren chairman becomes official
facts.detail: Dennis stepped away after 28 years leading the team, reflecting candidly on his combative reputation in the sport.

facts.headline: Riccardo Patrese is born
facts.detail: Patrese started a then-record 256 Grands Prix across a 16-season career for five different teams.

facts.headline: Prost wins his second home race
facts.detail: Alain Prost dominated the French GP at Paul Ricard for Renault, beating Nelson Piquet.

facts.headline: Hamilton becomes the first multiple winner of the Chinese GP
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton won from third on the grid, making F1 history at the circuit.

facts.headline: Jochen Rindt is born
facts.detail: Rindt remains the only driver to win the World Championship posthumously, after his fatal 1970 practice crash at Monza.

facts.headline: Tyrrell wins its first race as a constructor
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart triumphed at the Spanish GP after a fierce 70-lap battle with Jacky Ickx.

facts.headline: Button wins a dramatic rain-hit Chinese GP
facts.detail: Jenson Button charged from fifth on the grid to claim his second win of the season for McLaren.

facts.headline: Stewart gives March its first-ever win, lapping the entire field
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's dominant Spanish GP victory came in March's debut season as a constructor.

facts.headline: Vettel gives Red Bull its first-ever Formula One win
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel dominated the Chinese GP, a year after giving Toro Rosso its own maiden victory.

facts.headline: The Chinese GP is postponed as COVID-19 spreads
facts.detail: The scheduled fourth round of the 2020 season fell victim to the pandemic before the year's calendar was rebuilt from scratch.

facts.headline: Phil Hill is born
facts.detail: Hill remains one of only two American drivers to win the Formula One World Championship.

facts.headline: Hamilton leads lights-to-flag in China
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's dominant win from pole was followed home by Mercedes teammate Nico Rosberg for another 1-2.

facts.headline: Piastri takes his first championship points lead
facts.detail: Oscar Piastri's composed Saudi Arabian GP win moved him to the top of the standings for the first time in his career.

facts.headline: Senna wins his first Formula One race
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's maiden victory came at the Portuguese GP, marking the start of a legendary career.

facts.headline: Valentino Rossi tests a Ferrari F1 car
facts.detail: The MotoGP champion impressed at Fiorano, reportedly showing serious raw speed in his first laps.

facts.headline: Red Bull unveils its three-story paddock motorhome
facts.detail: The extravagant 'Energy Station' shocked and impressed the F1 paddock on its debut.

facts.headline: Top-level motorsport returns after World War II
facts.detail: The first major postwar Grand Prix was held in Nice, ending nearly seven years without top-flight racing.

facts.headline: F1 returns to Bahrain after a year's cancellation
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel led from pole to win the race, which had been scrapped in 2011 amid anti-government protests.

facts.headline: Stirling Moss's career-ending crash occurs at Goodwood
facts.detail: A misunderstanding with Graham Hill sent Moss's Lotus off track, leaving him with severe injuries that ended his F1 career.

facts.headline: Berger survives a fiery crash at Tamburello
facts.detail: Gerhard Berger's Ferrari slammed into the barriers and burst into flames at the San Marino GP; he escaped thanks to a quick rescue.

facts.headline: Coulthard wins a weather-chaos British GP
facts.detail: David Coulthard's early-season Silverstone win was overshadowed by severe storms that caused chaos off the track.

facts.headline: A steering failure ends Mike Taylor's F1 career
facts.detail: A welded steering column failed on Taylor's Lotus at 160mph during the Belgian GP.

facts.headline: Alonso calls San Marino his 'best win in F1 so far'
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso inherited the lead when Kimi Raikkonen's McLaren retired, and held on for Renault.

facts.headline: Red Bull scores its first 1-2 finish since 2016
facts.detail: Max Verstappen led home teammate Sergio Perez at the Emilia Romagna GP.

facts.headline: Michele Alboreto dies testing an Audi sports car
facts.detail: The five-time Grand Prix winner and former Ferrari driver died after a high-speed tyre blowout at the Lausitzring.

facts.headline: Ferrari teammates Villeneuve and Pironi fall out bitterly
facts.detail: Controversy over a disputed San Marino GP result fractured the relationship between Gilles Villeneuve and Didier Pironi, weeks before Villeneuve's death.

facts.headline: Prost tightens his grip on the championship
facts.detail: Alain Prost's commanding San Marino win came as Ayrton Senna's early title challenge began to fade.

facts.headline: Button wins his third race in four starts
facts.detail: Jenson Button's hard-fought Bahrain GP victory continued Brawn GP's fairytale start to the season.

facts.headline: Coulthard scores his only win of the 1998 season
facts.detail: David Coulthard beat Michael Schumacher at Imola while teammate Mika Hakkinen went on to dominate the year.

facts.headline: Johnny Dumfries is born
facts.detail: A distant cousin of Queen Elizabeth II and heir to a Scottish marquessate, Dumfries raced in F1 before winning Le Mans.

facts.headline: A rear wing failure kills spectators at the Spanish GP
facts.detail: Rolf Stommelen's car crashed over the barriers at Montjuic Park, killing a fireman and four spectators.

facts.headline: Frentzen wins his first Grand Prix on Ferrari's home soil
facts.detail: Heinz-Harald Frentzen held off Michael Schumacher at Imola after teammate Jacques Villeneuve's early lead slipped away.

facts.headline: Raikkonen extends his points lead with a Ferrari 1-2
facts.detail: Kimi Raikkonen's dominant Spanish GP win would prove to be his final victory of his title-defense season.

facts.headline: Lauda wins his first Formula One race
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's maiden victory came at the Spanish GP, finishing 35 seconds clear of Ferrari teammate Clay Regazzoni.

facts.headline: Villeneuve wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve made up for a lost debut win in Australia by claiming his maiden victory at the European GP.

facts.headline: Mercedes scores a fourth straight 1-2 finish
facts.detail: Valtteri Bottas led home Lewis Hamilton at the Azerbaijan GP for his fifth career win.

facts.headline: Rob Walker dies
facts.detail: The legendary privateer team owner's independent outfit challenged manufacturer-backed teams through the 1950s and 60s.

facts.headline: Hakkinen retires from the lead on the final lap
facts.detail: A clutch failure denied Mika Hakkinen victory in Spain, handing Michael Schumacher a win he called bittersweet.

facts.headline: McLaren receives a suspended race ban over 'Liegate'
facts.detail: The team was punished for misleading stewards at the Australian GP earlier in the season.

facts.headline: Roland Ratzenberger dies in qualifying at Imola
facts.detail: His fatal crash came a day before Ayrton Senna's death at the same race weekend, one of F1's darkest chapters.

facts.headline: F1 returns to a modified Imola a year after Senna and Ratzenberger's deaths
facts.detail: A new chicane was added at Tamburello, the corner where Senna had crashed the year before.

facts.headline: Senna and Prost preview a season of McLaren domination
facts.detail: The pair qualified nearly three seconds clear of the field at San Marino in the all-conquering MP4/4.

facts.headline: Ayrton Senna dies at the San Marino GP
facts.detail: Senna's fatal crash at Imola's Tamburello corner remains F1's most consequential loss, sparking sweeping safety reforms.

facts.headline: Motor racing's first fatal accident occurs
facts.detail: The Marquis de Montaignac lost control and inadvertently caused a crash that killed his mechanic, motorsport's earliest recorded fatality.

facts.headline: Senna dominates San Marino six years before his death
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna led start to finish, with teammate Alain Prost second, in a poignant echo of the tragedy to come at the same race.

facts.headline: Hunt is disqualified for a car 5/8ths of an inch too wide
facts.detail: James Hunt's Spanish GP win was stripped over a minor width infringement, handing victory to Niki Lauda.

facts.headline: Coulthard survives a plane crash
facts.detail: David Coulthard's private jet caught fire and made an emergency landing approaching Lyon; he escaped with cracked ribs.

facts.headline: Bobby Unser dies
facts.detail: The three-time Indy 500 winner was one of American motorsport's giants.

facts.headline: Ken Tyrrell is born
facts.detail: Tyrrell founded and managed the Tyrrell Racing Organisation, entering F1 in 1968 with Jackie Stewart as his lead driver.

facts.headline: Piquet closes the title gap to three points
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet's San Marino GP win narrowed Carlos Reutemann's championship lead.

facts.headline: Mansell dominates from start to finish in Spain
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell led every lap despite a heavy downpour, extending his dominant start to the 1992 season.

facts.headline: Wolfgang von Trips is born
facts.detail: Germany's most successful pre-Schumacher F1 driver was on course to become 1961 champion before dying at Monza that season.

facts.headline: Stewart wins by two full laps
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's Matra crossed the finish line at the Spanish GP two laps ahead of second-placed Bruce McLaren.

facts.headline: Pironi wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Didier Pironi led from the start and lapped all but two drivers at the Belgian GP for Ligier.

facts.headline: Prost is disqualified two hours after 'winning'
facts.detail: Alain Prost's San Marino GP victory was stripped when his McLaren was found two kilos underweight after running out of fuel.

facts.headline: Hill wins San Marino as Schumacher's brake fails
facts.detail: Damon Hill's Williams victory came as Michael Schumacher's Ferrari suffered a seized front-right brake.

facts.headline: Prost's F1 team is auctioned off
facts.detail: Twelve cars from the collapsed Prost Grand Prix team were sold in Paris, marking the end of an era.

facts.headline: Rene Dreyfus is born
facts.detail: One of the leading French drivers of the 1930s, Dreyfus won the 1930 Monaco GP.

facts.headline: Prost wins San Marino comfortably
facts.detail: Alain Prost's McLaren finished 14 seconds clear of Rene Arnoux's Ferrari.

facts.headline: Tommy Byrne is born
facts.detail: Byrne is still regarded as one of the most talented drivers who never fully realized his potential in F1.

facts.headline: Bandini's Ferrari crashes into flames at Monaco
facts.detail: Lorenzo Bandini's car struck a lamp post and caught fire while he battled for second place, trapping him beneath the wreckage.

facts.headline: Depailler wins his first Grand Prix at Monaco
facts.detail: Patrick Depailler's Tyrrell led Niki Lauda's Brabham home by 22 seconds after many near-misses.

facts.headline: Schumacher takes his 86th career win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's European GP victory at the Nurburgring reignited the title fight with Fernando Alonso.

facts.headline: Gilles Villeneuve dies
facts.detail: Villeneuve's fatal qualifying crash at Zolder was described by F1's medical chief as almost inevitable given his fearless style.

facts.headline: Andretti wins the start of the European leg
facts.detail: Mario Andretti's Lotus lapped all but four competitors at the Spanish GP.

facts.headline: The first-ever Miami Grand Prix is held
facts.detail: Max Verstappen won the inaugural race amid huge fanfare for F1's new Florida venue.

facts.headline: Ferrari withdraws a day after Villeneuve's death
facts.detail: John Watson won the Belgian GP for McLaren as the paddock mourned Gilles Villeneuve, killed in qualifying the day before.

facts.headline: Schumacher matches Mansell's record with a fifth straight win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's 200th Grand Prix start brought victory in Spain, equaling a 1992 record for wins to start a season.

facts.headline: Prost beats Williams teammate Hill by 16.8 seconds
facts.detail: Alain Prost's Spanish GP win came in an otherwise uneventful race apart from the internal title rivalry.

facts.headline: Brabham wins his first Grand Prix, and Australia's first
facts.detail: Jack Brabham's Cooper triumphed at Monaco, the first win for both a rear-engined car and an Australian driver.

facts.headline: Lorenzo Bandini dies from his Monaco burns
facts.detail: Bandini succumbed three days after his fiery crash, prompting major safety reforms at the circuit.

facts.headline: Rindt wins Monaco at the final corner
facts.detail: Jochen Rindt seized victory after leader Jack Brabham crashed into the barriers on the last lap.

facts.headline: Ferrari makes its racing debut
facts.detail: The Tipo 125 S ran at Piacenza, marking Enzo Ferrari's transition from Alfa Romeo team manager to constructor under his own name.

facts.headline: Lauda ends Ferrari's 20-year Monaco drought
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's win was also the first for the new Ferrari 312T.

facts.headline: Schumacher masters the wet to win by 53 seconds
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Monaco GP victory margin over Rubens Barrichello was one of the largest of the era.

facts.headline: F1 races for the first time after Jim Clark's death
facts.detail: The Spanish GP was held in the shadow of losing the two-time champion, who had led the championship the week before.

facts.headline: Senna wins his fourth straight race of the season
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's dominant Monaco victory extended his flying start to the 1991 championship.

facts.headline: Ferrari's team orders spark public backlash
facts.detail: Rubens Barrichello was ordered to let Michael Schumacher win the Austrian GP after outpacing him all weekend.

facts.headline: F1 holds its first-ever World Championship race
facts.detail: The British GP at Silverstone launched the FIA World Championship of Drivers.

facts.headline: Moss wins Monaco from start to finish
facts.detail: Stirling Moss capitalized on a rare off day for Juan Manuel Fangio, who recovered to finish behind.

facts.headline: Scheckter's title-winning season begins with victory
facts.detail: Jody Scheckter's Belgian GP win was the first of his eventual championship-winning campaign.

facts.headline: Senna sets one of the greatest qualifying laps ever
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's Monaco pole lap, 1.427 seconds faster than teammate Prost, is still regarded as a defining moment of car control.

facts.headline: Beltoise wins on the rain-soaked streets of Monaco
facts.detail: Jean-Pierre Beltoise's BRM won by over half a minute in one of the wettest Monaco GPs on record.

facts.headline: Mansell drives his final F1 race
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell retired from the Spanish GP with an undrivable McLaren, ending his F1 career.

facts.headline: Elio de Angelis dies testing at Paul Ricard
facts.detail: A rear wing failure caused his Brabham to cartwheel off the track at high speed.

facts.headline: Karl Wendlinger is left in a coma at Monaco practice
facts.detail: The crash came just two weeks after the deaths of Ratzenberger and Senna, deepening one of F1's darkest stretches.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins his first Monaco GP
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher capitalized on a first-corner crash between Hill and Hakkinen for the first of his five Monaco victories.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins Monaco as Hakkinen's challenge fades
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher led a Ferrari 1-2 after pole-sitter Mika Hakkinen's McLaren faltered.

facts.headline: Mosley says his departure could threaten FIA control of F1
facts.detail: Max Mosley made the claim amid a scandal over revelations about his private life.

facts.headline: Webber dominates Monaco from pole
facts.detail: Mark Webber led every lap for Red Bull ahead of teammate Sebastian Vettel.

facts.headline: Mansell and Senna scuffle in the pit lane
facts.detail: The pair tangled at Spa after Mansell's bold outside overtake attempt, then confronted each other afterward.

facts.headline: Mansell sets a record for consecutive season-opening wins
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's fifth straight victory came at San Marino, extending his dominant start to 1992.

facts.headline: Hackers alter Ferrari's website over team orders
facts.detail: Brazilian hackers changed a headline in protest of Ferrari's use of team orders to secure Schumacher's Austrian GP win.

facts.headline: Trintignant wins his second and final Monaco GP
facts.detail: Maurice Trintignant benefited from a race of attrition after early leaders hit trouble.

facts.headline: Hill wins his fifth and final Monaco GP
facts.detail: Graham Hill, nicknamed 'Mr. Monaco', won five of the seven races he entered at the circuit.

facts.headline: Reutemann wins a chaotic pile-up Monaco
facts.detail: Carlos Reutemann's Williams triumphed after a huge first-lap crash took out five cars and a late gearbox failure eliminated the leader.

facts.headline: Colin Chapman is born
facts.detail: The legendary Lotus founder led his team to seven constructors' championships and pioneered major F1 innovations.

facts.headline: Jack Brabham dies
facts.detail: The three-time champion, aged 88, was the last surviving F1 World Champion from the 1950s.

facts.headline: Panis wins Ligier's final F1 victory
facts.detail: Olivier Panis triumphed in a rain-soaked Monaco GP as Ligier's F1 story reached its last high point.

facts.headline: Niki Lauda dies
facts.detail: The three-time World Champion, who famously returned to racing weeks after his fiery 1976 Nurburgring crash, died in Austria.

facts.headline: Dietrich Mateschitz is born
facts.detail: The Red Bull co-founder later acquired Jaguar and Minardi to create Red Bull Racing and Toro Rosso.

facts.headline: Hill wins on his way to the 1962 title
facts.detail: Graham Hill led 69 of 80 laps at the European GP, the first of four wins that season.

facts.headline: Fangio wins F1's second-ever championship race
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio triumphed at Monaco despite waves and spray flooding parts of the harbour circuit.

facts.headline: Andretti leads a dominant Lotus 1-2
facts.detail: Mario Andretti's Belgian GP win, with Gilles Villeneuve initially second, was a familiar sight in Lotus's dominant 1978 season.

facts.headline: Villeneuve accuses Montoya of a dangerous move
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve said Juan Pablo Montoya's brake-testing tactics in a three-car pileup could have been fatal.

facts.headline: Ascari crashes into Monaco's harbour
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari's Lancia plunged into the water while battling for the lead; he escaped with minor injuries.

facts.headline: Stewart wins his second Grand Prix
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart won by 40 seconds at Monaco after John Surtees retired from the lead with a differential failure.

facts.headline: Scheckter wins Monaco for Wolf
facts.detail: Jody Scheckter overtook John Watson at the first corner and held off the Ferraris of Lauda and Reutemann.

facts.headline: Senna wins his sixth and final Monaco GP
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's fifth consecutive win at the principality set a new record for victories at the race.

facts.headline: Max Mosley dies
facts.detail: The former FIA president died at 81 after battling cancer.

facts.headline: Trulli ends Schumacher's dominant start to the season
facts.detail: Jarno Trulli led the Monaco GP from pole to flag for Renault, snapping Michael Schumacher's run of wins.

facts.headline: The Paris-Madrid Trial disaster ends open-road racing
facts.detail: More than 100 casualties in the chaotic 1903 race pushed motorsport toward specialized enclosed circuits.

facts.headline: Hakkinen wins his only Monaco GP
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen took pole, the win, and fastest lap in a dominant performance.

facts.headline: Clark wins comfortably in the Netherlands
facts.detail: Jim Clark's Lotus led from the first corner ahead of John Surtees' Ferrari.

facts.headline: Hamilton stages a comeback win at Monaco
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton recovered from hitting a barrier early on to beat Robert Kubica and Felipe Massa.

facts.headline: Villeneuve holds off a late charge from Panis
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve led the Spanish GP from start to finish despite tyre wear troubles.

facts.headline: Rosberg leads a Mercedes 1-2 at Monaco
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg won from pole ahead of teammate Lewis Hamilton, with Daniel Ricciardo third.

facts.headline: Ascari dies testing, four days after his Monaco harbour escape
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari was killed testing a Ferrari at Monza, an eerie postscript to surviving his plunge into the water days earlier.

facts.headline: Paul Hawkins dies in an eerie echo of Ascari's fate
facts.detail: Hawkins, the only other driver besides Ascari to survive a plunge into Monaco's harbour, was killed this day.

facts.headline: Leclerc wins his home race, ending his self-proclaimed curse
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc's Monaco GP victory came after years of misfortune at his home event.

facts.headline: Fangio wins brilliantly in appalling wet conditions
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio's fearless drive through the Swiss GP's fast bends cemented his growing reputation.

facts.headline: Schumacher's Monaco win is tainted by a pit-lane dispute
facts.detail: McLaren boss Ron Dennis denied threatening Enrique Bernoldi's career during a heated post-race row.

facts.headline: Webber's win makes it six different winners in six races
facts.detail: Mark Webber's Monaco victory set an unprecedented record for parity at the start of a season.

facts.headline: Senna equals Jim Clark's career pole record
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's Mexican GP pole matched Clark's long-standing mark of 33.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins Monaco with a one-stop strategy
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's single pit stop beat Damon Hill's two-stop approach from pole.

facts.headline: Coulthard podiums in a Superman cape
facts.detail: David Coulthard's Monaco third place, promoting a Hollywood film, ended a long podium absence for Red Bull.

facts.headline: Senna and Prost make the season look over after four races
facts.detail: Their dominant McLaren 1-2 at the Mexican GP led journalists to declare the title race effectively decided.

facts.headline: Moss wins for a privateer team at Monaco
facts.detail: Stirling Moss drove Rob Walker's Lotus 18 to victory as all 16 starters broke the previous lap record.

facts.headline: Mansell survives a scary crash at the Indy 500
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell was hit from behind under a yellow flag and his car filled with smoke before he emerged unhurt.

facts.headline: Bill Vukovich dies at the Indy 500
facts.detail: The two-time winner's fatal crash was the first fatality at a FIA World Championship event.

facts.headline: Eddie Sachs and Dave MacDonald die in a fiery Indy 500 crash
facts.detail: A seven-car pileup on lap two claimed both drivers' lives in one of the race's darkest days.

facts.headline: Lauda dominates Monaco for his fourth win in six races
facts.detail: Niki Lauda extended his championship lead with a commanding Ferrari victory.

facts.headline: BRM wins its first-ever championship race
facts.detail: The British team's breakthrough came at the Dutch GP after years of near-misses.

facts.headline: Villeneuve gives Ferrari its first win in a turbo car
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve's Monaco victory came after Piquet crashed and Jones suffered a fuel issue.

facts.headline: A loose wheel nut costs Mansell the win
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell was forced to pit while leading Monaco with eight laps left, handing victory to Senna.

facts.headline: Ron Dennis is born
facts.detail: Dennis rose from mechanic to McLaren team principal, CEO, and co-owner, shaping the team for nearly three decades.

facts.headline: Montoya wins his only Monaco GP
facts.detail: Juan Pablo Montoya beat Kimi Raikkonen by less than a second, the race decided during the pit stop phase.

facts.headline: Jaguar's Newey deal collapses at the last minute
facts.detail: Adrian Newey had appeared set to leave McLaren for Jaguar before Ron Dennis persuaded him to stay.

facts.headline: Bruce McLaren dies testing a Can-Am car
