facts.detail: The four-time Grand Prix winner and team founder died at Goodwood when bodywork failed at speed on the Lavant Straight.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins his first race for Ferrari in dominant rain
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Spanish GP victory, by 45 seconds, is remembered as one of his career-defining drives.

facts.headline: Mansell's premature celebration nearly costs him the win
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell waved to fans while still racing at the Canadian GP, an incident that became one of F1's most memorable mishaps.

facts.headline: Stewart ties Clark's win record
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's Monaco GP victory was his 25th career win, matching Jim Clark's tally.

facts.headline: Senna and Bellof chase down Prost in a legendary wet drive
facts.detail: Two of F1's brightest young talents closed rapidly on Alain Prost's lead at a rain-soaked Monaco before the race was stopped.

facts.headline: A transmission failure costs Fangio a near-certain win
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio had dominated the Belgian GP weekend before his car failed, handing victory to teammate Peter Collins.

facts.headline: The Cosworth DFV makes its championship debut
facts.detail: F1's most successful engine ever powered Jim Clark's Lotus 49 at the Dutch GP, pioneering four-valve-per-cylinder heads.

facts.headline: Coulthard wins his first Monaco GP
facts.detail: David Coulthard inherited the lead after Michael Schumacher retired with a cracked exhaust.

facts.headline: Prost wins as his main rivals retire
facts.detail: Alain Prost's US GP win in Phoenix came as both Senna and Mansell fell out of contention.

facts.headline: Patrick Head is born
facts.detail: Head co-founded Williams Grand Prix Engineering with Frank Williams in 1977 and became the team's Technical Director.

facts.headline: Fangio and Moss dominate a Mercedes 1-2 at Spa
facts.detail: The pair led home the Belgian GP despite Lancia's withdrawal from the championship weeks earlier.

facts.headline: Alboreto wins in Detroit
facts.detail: Michele Alboreto and Nelson Piquet outlasted rivals who pitted mid-race for tyres.

facts.headline: Switzerland overturns its 52-year ban on motor racing
facts.detail: The Swiss parliament voted to lift the ban imposed after the catastrophic 1955 Le Mans disaster.

facts.headline: Watson wins from 17th on the grid
facts.detail: John Watson's remarkable comeback drive at the inaugural Detroit GP remains one of F1's great recovery drives.

facts.headline: A fatal crash overshadows Brabham's Dutch GP win
facts.detail: Dan Gurney's BRM suffered brake failure, causing a crash that claimed a spectator's life during Jack Brabham's victory.

facts.headline: Ascari wins the Dutch GP from pole
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari triumphed on a resurfaced, deteriorating circuit amid tightly matched practice times.

facts.headline: Rodriguez wins as the title fight tightens
facts.detail: Pedro Rodriguez's Belgian GP victory narrowed the gap between championship rivals Brabham and Stewart.

facts.headline: A first-corner melee mars the Canadian GP
facts.detail: Alexander Wurz's daring move on Jean Alesi triggered a dramatic multi-car collision.

facts.headline: Ludovico Scarfiotti dies in a hill climb crash
facts.detail: The Italian driver's Porsche veered off the Rossfeldhohenringstrasse near Berchtesgaden.

facts.headline: Hamilton crashes into the back of a stationary car in the pit lane
facts.detail: A shocking error while leading the Canadian GP by over 7 seconds ended Lewis Hamilton's race.

facts.headline: Ricciardo wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Daniel Ricciardo charged from sixth to take a dramatic Canadian GP victory for Red Bull.

facts.headline: McLaren wins its first Formula One race
facts.detail: Bruce McLaren won the Belgian GP driving for the team he founded himself.

facts.headline: Scheckter wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Jody Scheckter's Tyrrell took the lead from teammate Patrick Depailler at the Swedish GP.

facts.headline: Ferrari records its 150th race win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher led home a Ferrari result at the Canadian GP with a one-stop strategy.

facts.headline: The Schumacher brothers finish 1-2 for the first time in Canada
facts.detail: Michael and Ralf Schumacher made history as the first siblings to finish first and second in F1.

facts.headline: Hamilton wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's Canadian GP victory came in just his sixth race, after podiums in every prior round.

facts.headline: Senna extends his championship lead in Canada
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's third win of the season was made easier by teammate Berger's one-lap penalty.

facts.headline: The deadliest accident in motorsport history occurs at Le Mans
facts.detail: Pierre Levegh's Mercedes collided with another car and disintegrated into the crowd, killing over 80 spectators.

facts.headline: Jackie Stewart is born
facts.detail: 'The Flying Scot' won three World Championships between 1965 and 1973.

facts.headline: Alesi wins his only F1 race, on his 31st birthday
facts.detail: Jean Alesi's emotional Canadian GP victory for Ferrari came on his 91st attempt, with fans breaking through barriers to celebrate.

facts.headline: One of F1's most dramatic races unfolds in Canada
facts.detail: Rain delays and multiple safety car periods turned the 2011 Canadian GP into an instant classic.

facts.headline: Schumacher extends his title lead to 28 points
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's fifth win in six races put Damon Hill in a hole he never recovered from.

facts.headline: A marshal is killed by a recovery crane at the Canadian GP
facts.detail: Volunteer marshal Mark Robinson died after being struck while helping clear a stranded car.

facts.headline: Tyrrell's six-wheeler wins its only race
facts.detail: Jody Scheckter's Swedish GP victory in the unique P34 broke Ferrari's nine-race winning streak.

facts.headline: Riccardo Paletti's death overshadows the Canadian GP
facts.detail: The rookie's fatal start-line crash cast a shadow over Nelson Piquet's win.

facts.headline: Hakkinen wins under a safety car after a dramatic crash
facts.detail: A safety car period, triggered by a Heinz-Harald Frentzen crash, made the margin of Hakkinen's win misleadingly small.

facts.headline: Two leaders run out of fuel on the final lap
facts.detail: Graham Hill and Dan Gurney both ran dry at the Belgian GP, handing a stunned Bruce McLaren the win.

facts.headline: Berger's win is held up for hours by a scrutineering dispute
facts.detail: A bolt on his McLaren's rear wing flap triggered a lengthy post-race investigation before his Canadian GP victory stood.

facts.headline: Hamilton wins his first race for Ferrari
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton ended Mercedes' unbeaten run and claimed his first win in nearly two years at the inaugural Barcelona-Catalunya GP.

facts.headline: James Hunt dies suddenly at 45
facts.detail: The 1976 World Champion died of a heart attack at his home in Wimbledon, shortly after his engagement.

facts.headline: Panis breaks both legs in a 160mph crash
facts.detail: Olivier Panis's violent collision with a wall stopped the Canadian GP with 14 laps remaining.

facts.headline: Britain sweeps the top of the podium at Spa
facts.detail: Tony Brooks led home Mike Hawthorn, Stuart Lewis-Evans, and Cliff Allison in a dominant British showing.

facts.headline: Alboreto leads a Ferrari 1-2 in Canada
facts.detail: Michele Alboreto beat Stefan Johansson with Alain Prost's McLaren just two seconds behind.

facts.headline: Hill wins as Schumacher's Ferrari stalls and retires
facts.detail: Damon Hill's Canadian GP victory came in a disastrous weekend for Michael Schumacher, who started from the back.

facts.headline: Mansell shatters lap records in a near-miss
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's spirited chase in Mexico fell just 1.3 seconds short of teammate Patrese's win.

facts.headline: Hulme ends a Stewart-Fittipaldi winning streak
facts.detail: Denny Hulme's Swedish GP win was unpopular with locals after he overtook their home favorite.

facts.headline: Lauda's win sparks a controversy over oversized cooling fans
facts.detail: Rivals claimed Niki Lauda's Brabham gained an unfair aerodynamic advantage from the fan device.

facts.headline: Bob Sweikert completes a unique motorsport triple crown
facts.detail: Sweikert won the Indianapolis 500, the National Championship, and the Midwest Sprint Car title all in one season.

facts.headline: Denny Hulme is born
facts.detail: New Zealand's only F1 World Champion, nicknamed 'The Bear', was admired throughout the paddock.

facts.headline: Gordon Murray is born
facts.detail: The engineering genius behind Brabham's radical fan car and McLaren's iconic F1 road car reshaped car design thinking.

facts.headline: Moss is seriously injured in a practice crash
facts.detail: Stirling Moss's Lotus rolled over a grass bank at Spa the day before the Belgian GP.

facts.headline: Two British drivers die in rapid succession at Spa
facts.detail: One of F1's darkest days saw fatal crashes claim two lives in poor conditions during the Belgian GP.

facts.headline: Only six cars start the US Grand Prix
facts.detail: Michelin tyre failures forced most teams to withdraw, badly damaging F1's reputation in America.

facts.headline: Senna wins as the Detroit track disintegrates
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's third win of the season came on an increasingly slippery, crumbling street circuit.

facts.headline: The FIA's precursor organization is founded
facts.detail: The AIACR was established in Paris, laying the groundwork for the modern FIA.

facts.headline: Luigi Fagioli dies from Monaco practice injuries
facts.detail: The Italian racer succumbed to injuries suffered crashing during practice for a sports car event.

facts.headline: Schumacher nearly withdraws after his brother's severe crash
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher considered pulling out of the US GP following Ralf Schumacher's violent accident, but went on to win.

facts.headline: Piers Courage dies at the Dutch GP
facts.detail: The 28-year-old Frank Williams Racing driver's car rolled and caught fire after leaving the track at Zandvoort.

facts.headline: Senna leaves the track to watch a World Cup match
facts.detail: After taking Detroit pole, Ayrton Senna recorded a lap commentary before heading off to watch France play Brazil.

facts.headline: Vettel leads start to finish at the British GP
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel's commanding Red Bull win came ahead of teammate Mark Webber and Brawn's Barrichello.

facts.headline: Louis Chiron dies
facts.detail: The most famous Monegasque driver before Charles Leclerc, Chiron's career spanned the eras before and after World War II.

facts.headline: Hesketh Racing signs James Hunt
facts.detail: Lord Hesketh's fledgling team built its early F1 credibility around Hunt as its lead driver.

facts.headline: BMW announces its move to buy Sauber
facts.detail: BMW ended its Williams engine partnership to acquire Sauber outright, forming BMW Sauber.

facts.headline: Stewart and Matra score a hat-trick of firsts
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's rain-soaked Dutch GP win was Matra's first, a French manufacturer's first, and Ken Tyrrell's first as an entrant.

facts.headline: Mazda wins Le Mans with a rotary engine
facts.detail: Drivers Johnny Herbert, Bertrand Gachot, and Volker Weidler gave a non-European manufacturer its first Le Mans win.

facts.headline: Clark breaks the 100mph barrier at Zandvoort
facts.detail: Jim Clark lapped the entire field en route to Lotus's tenth Grand Prix victory.

facts.headline: Juan Manuel Fangio is born
facts.detail: Widely regarded as the greatest driver of all time, Fangio won five World Championships and 24 races.

facts.headline: Montoya is banned from French roads for speeding
facts.detail: Juan Pablo Montoya was caught doing 126mph in his BMW, but the ban didn't stop him racing.

facts.headline: Piquet holds off rookie Brundle in Detroit
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet led from start to finish, narrowly staving off Martin Brundle's challenge in his debut season.

facts.headline: Dick Seaman dies at the Belgian GP
facts.detail: The British aristocrat crashed into a tree while leading, his car bursting into flames.

facts.headline: Alonso's fourth straight win nears him a second title
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso's Canadian GP victory for Renault extended his dominant championship form.

facts.headline: Johnny Herbert is born
facts.detail: Herbert went on to win three Grands Prix, including the 1995 British GP.

facts.headline: Ferrari is fined $1 million for a podium protocol violation
facts.detail: The penalty followed Barrichello letting Schumacher pass him to win the Austrian GP after already using team orders on track.

facts.headline: McLaren's new car fails a crash test again
facts.detail: The troubled MP4-18 project's repeated failures forced McLaren to continue racing an older chassis.

facts.headline: Mosley dismisses resignation calls after the US GP debacle
facts.detail: Max Mosley brushed off criticism following the Michelin tyre crisis that saw only six cars race at Indianapolis.

facts.headline: Nico Rosberg is born
facts.detail: The son of 1982 champion Keke Rosberg went on to win the 2016 World Championship himself.

facts.headline: Clark wins at Clermont-Ferrand
facts.detail: Jim Clark led a trio of British drivers home at the demanding French circuit.

facts.headline: Frentzen wins a wet, safety-car-affected French GP
facts.detail: Heinz-Harald Frentzen's Jordan capitalized on changing conditions for a surprise victory.

facts.headline: Gurney gives Brabham its first win as a constructor
facts.detail: Dan Gurney's French GP victory came with team owner Jack Brabham himself finishing third.

facts.headline: Mediobanca buys a 34% stake in Ferrari
facts.detail: The Italian banking giant's $768 million purchase from a financially struggling Fiat reshaped Ferrari's ownership.

facts.headline: Kubica downplays claims a Pope 'saved' his life
facts.detail: Robert Kubica expressed skepticism about reports linking Pope John Paul II to his survival of a severe Canadian GP crash.

facts.headline: Harry Schell, America's first F1 driver, is born
facts.detail: Schell never won a championship title but earned respect throughout the paddock for his race craft.

facts.headline: Jones beats seven home drivers at Paul Ricard
facts.detail: Alan Jones held off a strong French contingent including Laffite, Arnoux, and Pironi.

facts.headline: A late rain shower nearly costs Schumacher his lead
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher spun despite a substantial points lead as sudden rain caught out the field.

facts.headline: Giuseppe Farina, F1's first-ever champion, dies
facts.detail: Farina was killed in a road accident while driving to the French GP.

facts.headline: Ralf Schumacher is born
facts.detail: The younger Schumacher brother began racing on the family's go-kart track alongside Michael.

facts.headline: Clark wins commandingly at Reims
facts.detail: Jim Clark's Lotus-Climax beat Tony Maggs and Graham Hill at the French GP.

facts.headline: Peterson wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Ronnie Peterson's French GP victory came ahead of home favorite Francois Cevert.

facts.headline: Villeneuve and Arnoux fight an epic final-lap duel
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve and Rene Arnoux traded paint at the French GP in one of F1's most celebrated wheel-to-wheel battles, though Jabouille won.

facts.headline: Schumacher reaches his 50th career win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's French GP victory came against tough competition from pole-sitter brother Ralf.

facts.headline: Fangio wins the inaugural French GP as a championship round
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio led home teammates Fagioli and Whitehead at Reims-Gueux.

facts.headline: David Purley dies
facts.detail: The driver known for his heroic rescue attempt at the 1973 Dutch GP died in Bognor Regis.

facts.headline: Coulthard leads a McLaren 1-2 in France
facts.detail: David Coulthard beat teammate Mika Hakkinen after pole-sitter Schumacher fell back.

facts.headline: The French GP is cancelled after the Le Mans disaster
facts.detail: The catastrophic June crash that killed over 80 spectators forced the race off the calendar.

facts.headline: Sebastian Vettel is born
facts.detail: Vettel went on to win four consecutive World Championships with Red Bull.

facts.headline: McLaren's perfect season continues with another 1-2
facts.detail: Prost beat teammate Senna at the French GP as McLaren's MP4/4 dominated 1988.

facts.headline: Mercedes wins its first race as a constructor
facts.detail: Fangio led Karl Kling home at the French GP, debuting the team's striking streamlined bodywork.

facts.headline: Roland Ratzenberger is born
facts.detail: Ratzenberger's death at Imola in 1994 came a day before Ayrton Senna's, deepening F1's darkest weekend.

facts.headline: Stewart leads a Tyrrell 1-2 at his French home win
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart led teammate Francois Cevert, the home crowd's favorite, to victory.

facts.headline: A physical altercation ends Behra's Ferrari career
facts.detail: Jean Behra's fight with team manager Romolo Tavoni after the French GP ended his time at the team.

facts.headline: Prost wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Alain Prost's French GP victory came after a thrilling two-part race.

facts.headline: Ecclestone sparks outrage praising Hitler's ability to 'get things done'
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone's remarks in an interview drew global condemnation.

facts.headline: Musso dies chasing his own teammate for the lead
facts.detail: Luigi Musso crashed fatally at the French GP attempting to catch Mike Hawthorn.

facts.headline: Mansell wins as Senna spins out
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell overtook Ayrton Senna at the first corner of the French GP after Senna's pole-position spin.

facts.headline: Hamilton wins by over a minute in torrential rain
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton drove flawlessly from fourth on the grid at a chaotic British GP.

facts.headline: Jo Schlesser dies in Honda's experimental car
facts.detail: Schlesser became the fourth driver to die that season, trapped in his blazing RA302 despite Surtees' safety warnings.

facts.headline: F1 races at Magny-Cours for the first time
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell won the inaugural, widely praised race at the circuit that replaced Paul Ricard.

facts.headline: Mosley denies Nazi role-play claims in a tabloid sex scandal
facts.detail: The FIA president faced a court case over allegations published by the News of the World.

facts.headline: Gurney gives Porsche its first championship win
facts.detail: Dan Gurney fought through the field from the third row to win the French GP.

facts.headline: Mansell collapses pushing his car in Dallas heat
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell jumped out to push his stricken car after the deteriorating street circuit claimed his race.

facts.headline: Ecclestone proposes deciding grid positions by ballot
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone floated a random draw to inject unpredictability amid Schumacher's dominant season.

facts.headline: Prost wins the weekend after announcing his Ferrari move
facts.detail: Alain Prost's French GP win came just after confirming he'd leave McLaren for 1990.

facts.headline: Montoya turns his back on F1 for NASCAR
facts.detail: Juan Pablo Montoya signed with Chip Ganassi Racing a week after leaving McLaren.

facts.headline: Christian Horner is dismissed as Red Bull's team principal
facts.detail: Horner departed after 20 years leading the team to eight World Championships.

facts.headline: Clark wins his fourth consecutive British GP
facts.detail: Jim Clark held off a late Graham Hill charge to win by three seconds.

facts.headline: Senna wins as Mansell steals the show
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's wet British GP win was overshadowed by Nigel Mansell's crowd-thrilling charge to second.

facts.headline: Hill wins after his suspension fell apart on lap one of practice
facts.detail: Damon Hill recovered from a disastrous weekend start to win the British GP.

facts.headline: Pedro Rodriguez dies
facts.detail: The eccentric BRM driver, known for his deerstalker hat, died racing in Germany.

facts.headline: Prost claims his 50th Grand Prix win
facts.detail: Alain Prost capitalized on misfortune for both Hill and Senna at the British GP.

facts.headline: A rare brake failure ends Schumacher's title bid
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher broke his leg crashing at Stowe corner while attacking Eddie Irvine.

facts.headline: Mansell wins but runs out of fuel on his victory lap
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell passed teammate Piquet three laps from the end, then coasted to a stop celebrating.

facts.headline: Poor stewarding hands Schumacher a controversial win
facts.detail: A late-applied penalty let Michael Schumacher exploit the rules at the British GP.

facts.headline: Webber wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Mark Webber's German GP victory came despite a drive-through penalty for a first-corner clash.

facts.headline: Alberto Ascari is born
facts.detail: The double World Champion won six consecutive Grands Prix on his way to the 1952 title.

facts.headline: Jones extends his title lead in Britain
facts.detail: Alan Jones won by ten seconds over Nelson Piquet, growing his championship lead.

facts.headline: Villeneuve wins fortuitously as leaders retire
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve benefited when both Schumacher and Hakkinen were forced out of the British GP.

facts.headline: Two F1 drivers die in the same F2 race
facts.detail: Bill Whitehouse and Herbert Mackay-Fraser both died at Reims.

facts.headline: Williams wins its first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Clay Regazzoni, the oldest driver on the grid, gave the team its breakthrough win at its home British GP.

facts.headline: Ralf Schumacher becomes F1's fourth openly LGBTQ+ former driver
facts.detail: Schumacher introduced his partner in a heartfelt Instagram announcement.

facts.headline: Ferrari sweeps the podium in Britain
facts.detail: Wolfgang von Trips led Phil Hill and Richie Ginther to a 1-2-3 finish.

facts.headline: Clark revives his season with a British GP win
facts.detail: Jim Clark's Lotus overcame reliability troubles that had plagued the team's faster cars.

facts.headline: Prost's third straight win closes the title gap on Senna
facts.detail: Alain Prost's British GP victory came amid an early battle between Senna and Mansell.

facts.headline: A classic race follows the Le Mans tragedy's shadow
facts.detail: The British GP at Aintree provided a much-needed high point after the previous month's disaster.

facts.headline: A Hill-Schumacher collision gifts Herbert his first win
facts.detail: Johnny Herbert claimed a surprise British GP victory at his home race after the title rivals took each other out.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins the same Grand Prix for the eighth time
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's French GP victory was a record for repeat wins at a single race.

facts.headline: Juan Manuel Fangio dies
facts.detail: Widely hailed as the greatest driver ever, Fangio died in Buenos Aires at 84.

facts.headline: Jules Bianchi dies from his Japanese GP injuries
facts.detail: Bianchi's death, nine months after his crash, made him F1's first fatality in 21 years.

facts.headline: Verstappen wins F1's first-ever Sprint race
facts.detail: Max Verstappen beat Lewis Hamilton after a decisive launch at the British GP.

facts.headline: A British GP result stays unresolved for over two months
facts.detail: The controversial 1976 race wasn't officially decided until late September.

facts.headline: Watson gives McLaren an unexpected win
facts.detail: John Watson caught the faster turbocharged Renaults as their reliability faltered.

facts.headline: F1 introduces Sprint Qualifying for the first time
facts.detail: The British GP hosted the format's debut, a 100km Saturday race deciding grid order.

facts.headline: Collins wins amid Ferrari turmoil
facts.detail: Peter Collins triumphed at Silverstone weeks after Enzo Ferrari controversially demoted him within the team.

facts.headline: Stewart edges Rindt in an epic battle
facts.detail: Jochen Rindt's two pit stops for repairs let Jackie Stewart take the British GP.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi is declared winner while sitting in the pits
facts.detail: A red-flagged, rain-hit British GP produced one of F1's strangest race conclusions.

facts.headline: Moss and Brooks give Britain its first home car win
facts.detail: Stirling Moss and Tony Brooks shared a historic Vanwall victory at Aintree.

facts.headline: Chris Amon is born
facts.detail: Widely regarded as the greatest driver never to win a championship Grand Prix.

facts.headline: A defrocked priest runs onto the Silverstone track mid-race
facts.detail: Cornelius Horan's protest run onto the Hangar Straight caused a red flag in one of F1's strangest incidents.

facts.headline: Clark wins his first British GP
facts.detail: Jim Clark took pole, victory, and fastest lap at a crowded Aintree.

facts.headline: Schumacher matches Fangio's five-title record
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher clinched the championship with a record six races still remaining.

facts.headline: Prost beats Senna after his Lotus runs dry
facts.detail: Alain Prost's British GP win came as Ayrton Senna's fuel-starved car fell back late.

facts.headline: Barrichello breaks his own trophy at the airport
facts.detail: Rubens Barrichello's gold British GP trophy was accidentally knocked to the ground while checking in for his flight.

facts.headline: Lauda beats Prost to narrow the title gap
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's British GP win over his McLaren teammate tightened the championship fight.

facts.headline: Ecclestone defends Schumacher's record-chasing dominance
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone pushed back against critics who called the sport boring.

facts.headline: Verstappen wins his seventh consecutive race
facts.detail: Max Verstappen's Hungarian GP victory extended a record-breaking winning streak.

facts.headline: Button announces his move to BAR
facts.detail: Jenson Button left Renault seeking a fresh opportunity to progress his career.

facts.headline: Briatore signs on to play himself in an Italian film
facts.detail: The flamboyant Renault boss took a cameo role set around his Sardinian nightclub.

facts.headline: Seaman wins the German GP with Hitler watching
facts.detail: British aristocrat Dick Seaman's Mercedes victory at the Nurburgring came under the eyes of the Nazi leadership.

facts.headline: Senna beats Prost as McLaren marches toward the title
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's German GP win was one of eight straight for the dominant MP4/4.

facts.headline: Alonso extends his championship lead to 36 points
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso's German GP win came as title rival Raikkonen fell away.

facts.headline: Renault scores its first-ever 1-2 finish
facts.detail: Rene Arnoux led teammate Alain Prost home at the French GP, the manufacturer's tenth win.

facts.headline: Prost wins his 51st and final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Alain Prost's German GP victory strengthened his grip on a fourth title before retirement.

facts.headline: Team orders spark controversy at Ferrari
facts.detail: Felipe Massa was instructed to hand the lead, and the win, to Fernando Alonso in Germany.

facts.headline: Antonio Ascari dies leading the French GP
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari's father crashed fatally at Montlhery, leaving behind a seven-year-old son who'd become a double champion himself.

facts.headline: Mansell wins in front of Schumacher's home crowd
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell dominated the German GP despite massive crowds cheering for the young Michael Schumacher.

facts.headline: Hamilton takes his tenth career win
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton charged from fourth on the grid to win the Hungarian GP.

facts.headline: Prost pushes his fuel-starved car toward the finish
facts.detail: Alain Prost jumped out to shove his stricken McLaren after running dry on the final lap.

facts.headline: Berger wins his final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Gerhard Berger's emotional German GP victory was Benetton's 27th and final win as a team.

facts.headline: Ricciardo wins an unpredictable weather-hit Hungarian GP
facts.detail: Daniel Ricciardo's Red Bull capitalized on safety cars and shifting strategy gambles.

facts.headline: Nuvolari upsets the Nazi-backed German teams
facts.detail: Against Hitler's expectations of a Mercedes or Auto Union sweep, an Italian driver won the German GP.

facts.headline: Hill matches Schumacher's career win tally
facts.detail: Damon Hill's German GP win was his 20th, equaling Michael Schumacher's total at the time.

facts.headline: Schumacher matches the record for wins in a season
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's German GP victory equaled his and Mansell's nine-win single-season record.

facts.headline: The Nurburgring hosts its first championship race
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari's German GP win was his first world championship victory for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Roger Williamson dies at the Dutch GP
facts.detail: The young British driver was killed after a tyre failure, despite fellow driver David Purley's desperate rescue attempts.

facts.headline: Fernando Alonso is born
facts.detail: Alonso began kart racing at age three, going on to win two World Championships.

facts.headline: A disgruntled employee runs onto the track mid-race
facts.detail: A former Mercedes worker cut through the fence at the German GP to stage a dangerous protest.

facts.headline: Senna leads a McLaren-dominant podium
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna led Prost and Mansell home at the German GP, mirroring the qualifying order.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins his fourth home race
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher dominated the German GP in front of his home fans.

facts.headline: Onofre Marimon becomes the first driver to die at a championship weekend
facts.detail: The Argentine driver's fatal practice crash at the German GP was a first for the World Championship era.

facts.headline: Lauda wins a year after his fiery Nurburgring crash
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's triumphant German GP victory came almost exactly a year after nearly dying at the same track.

facts.headline: A pit-lane fire engulfs Jos Verstappen's car
facts.detail: A fuel-rig malfunction sprayed fuel onto Verstappen's Benetton during a routine stop, igniting a terrifying blaze.

facts.headline: Lauda nearly dies in a fiery Nurburgring crash
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's Ferrari burst into flames after veering off track at the German GP; he received last rites but survived.

facts.headline: Clark clinches his second World Championship
facts.detail: Jim Clark's German GP win was his sixth of the season, wrapped up with plenty of races to spare.

facts.headline: Patrick Depailler dies in private testing
facts.detail: A suspension failure on his Alfa Romeo caused a fatal crash ten days before the German GP.

facts.headline: Carel Godin de Beaufort dies practicing at the Nurburgring
facts.detail: The Dutch nobleman crashed at the Bergwerk corner ahead of the German GP.

facts.headline: Drivers boycott the Nurburgring over safety concerns
facts.detail: The German GP moved to Hockenheim at the last minute after drivers refused to race at the old circuit.

facts.headline: Piastri publicly denies Alpine's driver announcement
facts.detail: Oscar Piastri's tweet refuting his own team's confirmation for 2023 became one of F1's most memorable driver-market moments.

facts.headline: Peter Collins dies chasing Tony Brooks
facts.detail: Collins crashed fatally at the Nurburgring's Pflanzgarten section while pushing to catch the leader.

facts.headline: Montoya completes a hat-trick in Germany
facts.detail: Juan Pablo Montoya took pole, fastest lap, and victory, overshadowing Schumacher's home race.

facts.headline: The Crashgate scandal begins with Piquet Jr's sacking
facts.detail: Renault's dismissal of Nelson Piquet Jr. set off revelations of a deliberately staged crash the previous season.

facts.headline: Fangio delivers one of his most legendary drives
facts.detail: After a poor pit stop left him over a minute down, Juan Manuel Fangio fought back to win the German GP.

facts.headline: Stewart wins what's regarded as his career-best drive
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart mastered fog and torrential rain at the Nurburgring in a race that nearly didn't happen.

facts.headline: Surtees wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: John Surtees benefited from Jim Clark's engine trouble to take his first F1 victory for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Fangio dominates by 46 seconds
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio's Ferrari crushed the field at the Nurburgring, taking pole and fastest lap too.

facts.headline: Button's Williams deal sparks a contract dispute
facts.detail: BAR-Honda claimed Jenson Button was in breach of contract after he signed with Williams for 2005.

facts.headline: Hamilton extends his rookie podium streak
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's Hungarian GP win was his tenth podium in his debut season.

facts.headline: Moss beats the Ferrari duo
facts.detail: Stirling Moss's Lotus-Climax outpaced von Trips and Hill at the German GP.

facts.headline: Button finally wins his first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Starting 14th, Jenson Button navigated a wet Hungarian GP for a long-awaited breakthrough.

facts.headline: Hulme leads a Brabham 1-2
facts.detail: Denny Hulme beat team owner Jack Brabham at the German GP as Jim Clark dominated practice.

facts.headline: Brooklands hosts its final race
facts.detail: The historic British circuit's last event went unnoticed as such at the time.

facts.headline: McLaren clinches the Constructors' title with a tenth 1-2
facts.detail: Senna and Prost's dominant season secured the championship with a record points haul.

facts.headline: F2 cars race alongside F1 to fill a thin grid
facts.detail: Organizers allowed smaller-category cars into the German GP due to a shortage of entries.

facts.headline: Nigel Mansell is born
facts.detail: The 1992 World Champion went on to win 31 races across 187 starts.

facts.headline: Salazar and Piquet collide, sparking a famous confrontation
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet punched Eliseo Salazar after their collision at the German GP in one of F1's most infamous scuffles.

facts.headline: Frentzen is sacked mid-season
facts.detail: Eddie Jordan replaced Heinz-Harald Frentzen with old friend Jean Alesi partway through the year.

facts.headline: Patrick Depailler is born
facts.detail: Depailler won twice in F1 before his career, and later his life, ended in accidents.

facts.headline: A loose wheel nut costs Mansell a commanding lead
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell was forced to retire from the Hungarian GP despite dominating.

facts.headline: McLaren denies Hamilton swore at Ron Dennis over the radio
facts.detail: Reports of a heated qualifying exchange were pushed back on by the team.

facts.headline: Laffite wins by three seconds
facts.detail: Jacques Laffite's Ligier held off the field at the German GP.

facts.headline: Prost's 100th start ends in retirement
facts.detail: Alain Prost's milestone race at the Hungarian GP was overshadowed by a lap-23 exit.

facts.headline: A hydraulics failure denies Hill an unlikely win
facts.detail: Damon Hill had led most of the Hungarian GP in an underpowered Arrows before the late heartbreak.

facts.headline: Jean Bugatti dies testing a car
facts.detail: The famed designer and engineer swerved to avoid a cyclist and struck a tree at just 30 years old.

facts.headline: Nuvolari is hailed as the greatest driver ever
facts.detail: Ferdinand Porsche's tribute cemented Tazio Nuvolari's legendary pre-war reputation.

facts.headline: Senna wins from pole in Hungary
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna led home the Williams pair of Mansell and Patrese.

facts.headline: Charlie Whiting is born
facts.detail: Whiting rose from Brabham chief mechanic to become F1's long-serving Race Director.

facts.headline: Manfred Winkelhock dies at Mosport Park
facts.detail: The former F1 driver was killed in a sports car endurance race crash.

facts.headline: Jones wins his third straight race for Williams
facts.detail: Alan Jones' Austrian GP victory extended a dominant streak for the team.

facts.headline: Peterson wins his final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Ronnie Peterson, often called one of the best never to win a title, took his last career victory in Austria.

facts.headline: Mansell's opportunistic pass on Senna wins him the race
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's daring overtake at the Hungarian GP remains one of F1's most celebrated moves.

facts.headline: Hill leads a Williams 1-2
facts.detail: Damon Hill's straightforward Hungarian GP win came with teammate Coulthard following him home.

facts.headline: Enzo Ferrari dies
facts.detail: The founder of Ferrari passed away peacefully in Maranello at age 90.

facts.headline: Shadow scores its only F1 victory
facts.detail: The team that gave Revson, Jarier, and Pryce their starts finally won a race.

facts.headline: Prost extends his championship lead
facts.detail: Alain Prost's Austrian GP win pulled him further ahead of Nelson Piquet, though Piquet took the title.

facts.headline: Schumacher breaks his own single-season win record
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's 82nd career victory in Hungary extended his own record for wins in a season.

facts.headline: De Angelis wins his first race by a whisker
facts.detail: Elio de Angelis's maiden victory in Austria came in one of F1's closest-ever finishes.

facts.headline: Watson wins Penske's only Grand Prix
facts.detail: John Watson's maiden victory, legend has it, came after he shaved off his mustache for luck.

facts.headline: Mansell finally becomes World Champion
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell clinched the title he'd long chased by finishing second in Hungary to Senna.

facts.headline: Laffite wins in Austria
facts.detail: Jacques Laffite's Ligier-Matra beat compatriot Rene Arnoux and Nelson Piquet.

facts.headline: Schumacher narrows the title gap to seven points
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Hungarian GP win closed in on championship leader Hakkinen.

facts.headline: Nelson Piquet is born
facts.detail: The three-time World Champion won his final title with Williams in 1987.

facts.headline: Brambilla wins his only race, and celebrates by crashing
facts.detail: Vittorio Brambilla's maiden Austrian GP win famously ended with him crashing while waving to the crowd.

facts.headline: Ferrari sweeps the podium in the Netherlands
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari led Giuseppe Farina and Luigi Villoresi to a 1-2-3 finish.

facts.headline: F1 races at Pescara, its longest-ever circuit
facts.detail: Stirling Moss won the inaugural, one-off Pescara GP after Belgium and the Netherlands dropped off the calendar.

facts.headline: 'Andrea de Crasheris' lives up to his nickname
facts.detail: Andrea de Cesaris added another spectacular accident to his reputation at the Austrian GP.

facts.headline: Barrichello leads a Ferrari 1-2 that secures the Constructors' title
facts.detail: Rubens Barrichello's Hungarian GP win clinched another championship for the dominant team.

facts.headline: Schumacher clinches his fourth title
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher led home teammate Barrichello at the Hungarian GP in a record-breaking Ferrari weekend.

facts.headline: Peterson wins in Austria
facts.detail: Ronnie Peterson's victory came as Emerson Fittipaldi's title hopes dimmed.

facts.headline: Lauda delights the home crowd
facts.detail: Niki Lauda climbed from fourth to win his home Austrian GP.

facts.headline: The last major pre-WWII Grand Prix is held in Switzerland
facts.detail: The 1939 Swiss GP at Bremgarten was split into two heats to entice Italian entries against dominant German teams.

facts.headline: Schumacher returns to driving after breaking his leg
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher took steps in his recovery at Ferrari's Mugello test track.

facts.headline: Badoer is called up after a decade away from racing
facts.detail: Ferrari's test driver Luca Badoer replaced the seriously injured Felipe Massa.

facts.headline: The Swiss GP is cancelled after the Le Mans disaster
facts.detail: The tragedy from earlier that summer forced the race off the calendar entirely.

facts.headline: A brutal F3000 crash nearly ends Herbert's career
facts.detail: Johnny Herbert's legs were badly injured at Brands Hatch, narrowly avoiding amputation.

facts.headline: F1 debuts in Turkey
facts.detail: The inaugural Turkish GP in Istanbul was an immediate success, won by Kimi Raikkonen.

facts.headline: Fangio wins at Bremgarten for Mercedes
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio held off Moss and the Ferraris of Hawthorn and Gonzalez.

facts.headline: Jordan and Trulli sign Fisichella in a driver swap
facts.detail: Giancarlo Fisichella and Jarno Trulli traded seats between Benetton and Jordan for 2002.

facts.headline: Ascari defies team orders to clinch his second title
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari led a Ferrari 1-2-3 finish in Switzerland to secure the championship.

facts.headline: Pironi's defiance of team orders becomes F1 legend
facts.detail: Didier Pironi ignored Ferrari's instructions to seize victory from Gilles Villeneuve, fracturing their partnership weeks before Villeneuve's death.

facts.headline: Justin Wilson dies from a track debris impact
facts.detail: The former F1 driver was struck by flying wreckage during an IndyCar race at Pocono.

facts.headline: Alonso becomes the youngest-ever Grand Prix winner
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso, 22, took the record with his maiden Hungarian GP victory for Renault.

facts.headline: Moss closes the title gap on Hawthorn
facts.detail: Stirling Moss's Portuguese GP win came in a somber weekend following Peter Collins' death.

facts.headline: Valencia hosts its first Grand Prix
facts.detail: Felipe Massa won the inaugural European GP on the new street circuit.

facts.headline: Lauda wins his 25th and final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's Dutch GP victory for McLaren was the last of his three-time-champion career.

facts.headline: Ken Tyrrell dies
facts.detail: The founder of the Tyrrell Racing Organisation, who entered F1 with Jackie Stewart in 1968, passed away.

facts.headline: Schumacher recovers from a heavy practice crash to win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher qualified third and fought back after a hard Friday shunt at the Belgian GP.

facts.headline: Villeneuve suffers a dramatic tyre failure
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve's Ferrari nearly disintegrated after a blowout while Alan Jones took his fourth straight win.

facts.headline: Senna beats Prost by four seconds
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's fifth win of the season at the Belgian GP came ahead of the reigning champion's Ferrari.

facts.headline: Cadillac confirms its first-ever F1 driver lineup
facts.detail: Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas were announced for the team's 2026 debut season.

facts.headline: The Canadian GP joins the World Championship
facts.detail: Jack Brabham won the first Canadian GP to count toward the title, in his own car.

facts.headline: Andretti wins the final race of his career
facts.detail: Mario Andretti's Dutch GP victory came in the same year he won the World Championship.

facts.headline: Senna narrowly beats Prost in Belgium
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's pole-to-flag win came with his French teammate close behind.

facts.headline: Phil Hill dies
facts.detail: America's first F1 World Champion, who won the 1961 title, had a complex and deeply thoughtful relationship with racing.

facts.headline: Schumacher is disqualified for an illegal wooden plank
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Belgian GP win was stripped after his Benetton showed excessive wear on its skid block.

facts.headline: Mike Parkes dies
facts.detail: The British driver, engineer, and designer had competed in F1 during the mid-1960s.

facts.headline: James Hunt is born
facts.detail: The 1976 World Champion lived a famously stormy life both on and off the track.

facts.headline: Hunt wins on his own birthday
facts.detail: James Hunt's Dutch GP victory came on the same day he turned 29.

facts.headline: F1 holds its shortest-ever championship race
facts.detail: A rain-shortened Belgian GP set the record for shortest race by both distance and laps completed.

facts.headline: Bruce McLaren is born
facts.detail: The New Zealander founded the team that remains one of F1's most successful constructors.

facts.headline: Schumacher gives Germany its first win in 17 years
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Belgian GP victory was the first by a German driver since Jochen Mass in 1975.

facts.headline: Hill gives Jordan its first-ever Grand Prix win
facts.detail: Damon Hill led home teammate Ralf Schumacher in a chaotic Belgian GP.

facts.headline: Piquet wins his second Grand Prix
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet's Dutch GP victory built on his first win earlier that season.

facts.headline: The Belgian GP is cancelled over a tobacco advertising dispute
facts.detail: The race was pulled from the calendar amid a standoff that briefly threatened the event's long-term future.

facts.headline: Stefan Bellof dies attempting a daring overtake at Eau Rouge
facts.detail: The rising star crashed fatally during a sportscar race at Spa, cutting short a career many thought destined for F1 stardom.

facts.headline: Leclerc becomes the first Monaco-born driver to win a Grand Prix
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc's Belgian GP victory came ahead of the Mercedes pair of Hamilton and Bottas.

facts.headline: Leclerc wins on Ferrari's home turf at Monza
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc held off McLaren's Oscar Piastri for a hugely popular Italian GP win.

facts.headline: Moss wins the race, but Fangio wins the title
facts.detail: Stirling Moss took the Italian GP while Juan Manuel Fangio's points tally secured the championship.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins Belgium as the newly crowned champion
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's win came after clinching his fourth title.

facts.headline: Hamilton and Vettel collide fighting for the lead
facts.detail: The two title rivals came together at the Italian GP, with Hamilton recovering to win.

facts.headline: Farina wins F1's first-ever Drivers' Championship
facts.detail: Giuseppe Farina's Italian GP victory secured the inaugural title, three points ahead of Fangio.

facts.headline: Ferdinand Porsche is born
facts.detail: The brilliant engineer founded the Porsche car company and designed some of motorsport's most significant early machines.

facts.headline: Hamilton breaks Schumacher's career pole record
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's 69th pole position at Monza surpassed Michael Schumacher's long-standing mark.

facts.headline: Ferrari sweeps the podium at Monza
facts.detail: Phil Hill led a 1-2-3 finish with teammates Ginther and Mairesse.

facts.headline: The FIA announces Crashgate charges against Renault
facts.detail: The formal charge followed Nelson Piquet Jr.'s claims of a deliberately staged 2008 crash.

facts.headline: Every car that starts the race finishes it
facts.detail: The Italian GP became only the second time in F1 history with a 100% finishing rate.

facts.headline: Rindt becomes F1's only posthumous World Champion
facts.detail: Jochen Rindt died in practice at Monza, but his points lead held up to secure the 1970 title.

facts.headline: Fangio wins at Monza for Mercedes
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio beat a trio of Ferraris after early leaders Kling and Hawthorn fell away.

facts.headline: Lotus withdraws a year after Rindt's death
facts.detail: Legal disputes with Italian authorities kept the team out of the Italian GP, though Regazzoni still starred for Ferrari.

facts.headline: Sid Watkins is born
facts.detail: The neurosurgeon became F1's revered chief medical officer, transforming safety and driver care in the sport.

facts.headline: Surtees wins on his way to becoming the only two-and-four-wheel champion
facts.detail: John Surtees' Italian GP win for Ferrari was a key step toward his unique double.

facts.headline: Hamilton achieves his second career grand slam
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton took pole, win, fastest lap, and led every lap of the Italian GP.

facts.headline: Stewart wins F1's most thrilling finish, by 0.08 seconds
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart edged Jochen Rindt in what The Times called the most exciting Grand Prix finish ever witnessed.

facts.headline: Lauda clinches his first World Championship
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's third-place finish at Monza was enough to secure the title as teammate Regazzoni won the race.

facts.headline: Hamilton is stripped of a Belgian GP win
facts.detail: Stewards ruled Lewis Hamilton gained an unfair advantage passing Raikkonen, handing the win to Massa.

facts.headline: Schumacher's Benetton move is announced
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's shock switch from Jordan blindsided his original team just a race after his debut.

facts.headline: Schumacher ends Ferrari's seven-year home drought
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Italian GP win thrilled the Tifosi after years of home disappointment.

facts.headline: Leclerc gives Ferrari its first Monza win since 2010
facts.detail: Charles Leclerc held off the Mercedes of Bottas to delight the home crowd.

facts.headline: F1 holds its first-ever all-turbo race
facts.detail: Tyrrell's expulsion for running underweight cars left the Italian GP grid entirely turbocharged.

facts.headline: Alonso becomes the first Spanish winner of the Italian GP
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso led a McLaren 1-2, cutting Hamilton's championship lead to three points.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi's title bid falls short at Monza
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi needed a win and Stewart to score nothing, but neither happened.

facts.headline: Three drivers die at Monza in one of racing's darkest days
facts.detail: Giuseppe Campari and two others were killed across the heats of the 1933 Italian GP.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi is crowned World Champion
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi's Italian GP win sealed the title with races to spare.

facts.headline: Schumacher equals Senna's win record
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's 41st career victory matched Ayrton Senna's tally in a head-to-head battle with Hakkinen.

facts.headline: Ronnie Peterson dies from complications after his Monza crash
facts.detail: The beloved Swedish driver's death devastated the F1 community.

facts.headline: Fangio caps his championship season with a Mercedes 1-2
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio led Piero Taruffi home at Monza.

facts.headline: Ferrari wins the race after Enzo Ferrari's death
facts.detail: Gerhard Berger led Michele Alboreto to a poignant 1-2 finish weeks after the founder's passing.

facts.headline: Lauda returns to the cockpit five weeks after nearly dying
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's heroic comeback race came shortly after receiving last rites following his Nurburgring crash.

facts.headline: Sid Watkins dies
facts.detail: F1's transformative chief medical officer, who served for over two decades, passed away at 84.

facts.headline: Alonso gives Ferrari its first home win in four years
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso's Italian GP victory ended a home-soil drought for the team.

facts.headline: Fangio spoils Ferrari's home party
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio snatched a dramatic victory from the Ferrari trio at Monza.

facts.headline: Mansell announces his F1 retirement
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell revealed he was leaving the sport, dissatisfied with Williams's contract negotiations.

facts.headline: Brawn GP wins its final race
facts.detail: Rubens Barrichello's Italian GP victory was the team's fourth and last 1-2 finish before becoming Mercedes.

facts.headline: Villeneuve survives a horrific crash at Imola
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve's bravery in a terrifying accident earned him widespread admiration.

facts.headline: Vettel becomes the youngest Grand Prix winner ever
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel, 21, won the Italian GP for Toro Rosso, a record at the time.

facts.headline: Hakkinen announces a sabbatical he never returns from
facts.detail: The double champion stepped aside for Kimi Raikkonen, ending his F1 career quietly.

facts.headline: Zanardi loses both legs in a horrific CART crash
facts.detail: Alex Zanardi miraculously survived the accident in Germany, later returning to competition as a Paralympic champion.

facts.headline: Senna wins with four champions filling the top five
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's Belgian GP victory came ahead of a star-studded podium of past and future title winners.

facts.headline: Gasly scores a surprise maiden win
facts.detail: Pierre Gasly became the first French winner since Panis in 1996, taking a shock Italian GP victory for AlphaTauri.

facts.headline: The Italian GP goes ahead under the shadow of 9/11
facts.detail: The race, held just five days after the attacks, saw serious discussion of cancellation before proceeding.

facts.headline: Briatore resigns amid the Crashgate fallout
facts.detail: Flavio Briatore stepped down as Renault boss as the staged-crash scandal spiraled.

facts.headline: Ascari beats Fangio at Monza
facts.detail: Alberto Ascari's win cut into Fangio's championship advantage.

facts.headline: Stirling Moss is born
facts.detail: Moss remains one of the most famous names in motorsport despite never winning the World Championship.

facts.headline: Damon Hill is born
facts.detail: Hill later became champion himself, following in father Graham's title-winning footsteps.

facts.headline: Schumacher backs down from skipping the US GP
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone warned Michael Schumacher he risked losing his title if he followed through on a post-9/11 boycott threat.

facts.headline: Charles de Tornaco dies practicing
facts.detail: The Belgian aristocrat rolled his Ferrari ahead of the Modena GP.

facts.headline: Panis retires after a 12-year F1 career
facts.detail: Olivier Panis's sole win came at Monaco in 1996, in what became a memorable underdog story.

facts.headline: Giancarlo Minardi is born
facts.detail: Minardi founded the beloved underdog team that gave many future stars their F1 debut.

facts.headline: Stewart clinches the title with his sixth win of the season
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's Canadian GP victory secured the championship for Tyrrell.

facts.headline: Cristiano da Matta is born
facts.detail: Da Matta later found success in CART before a brief F1 stint.

facts.headline: Ferenc Szisz, the first-ever Grand Prix winner, is born
facts.detail: Szisz won the inaugural 1906 French GP for Renault after starting as a riding mechanic.

facts.headline: Prost surpasses Stewart's career win record
facts.detail: Alain Prost's 28th victory at the Portuguese GP broke Jackie Stewart's long-standing mark.

facts.headline: Ickx leads a Brabham 1-2 in Canada
facts.detail: Jacky Ickx won from pole ahead of team owner Jack Brabham.

facts.headline: The first French GP after World War II is held
facts.detail: Racing's post-war resumption at Lyons was won by Monaco-born Louis Chiron despite pre-war equipment shortages.

facts.headline: Mansell scores what's called the most important win of his career
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's Portuguese GP victory set him up for a genuine title shot.

facts.headline: Trulli stuns in only his 14th Grand Prix
facts.detail: Jarno Trulli's standout weekend overshadowed Villeneuve's tenth career win.

facts.headline: Mansell's title bid ends in near-farce
facts.detail: A pit-lane wheel mix-up compounded Nigel Mansell's heartbreak at the Portuguese GP.

facts.headline: Villeneuve pulls off one of the season's most breathtaking overtakes
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve passed Michael Schumacher around the outside in a move still celebrated today.

facts.headline: Vettel achieves his most statistically dominant win
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel took pole, led every lap, set fastest lap, and won the Singapore GP by a huge margin.

facts.headline: Confusion reigns over Revson's Canadian GP win
facts.detail: It took over ten minutes after the checkered flag for officials to confirm Peter Revson's victory.

facts.headline: Mansell dispels retirement rumors with a brilliant win
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's Portuguese GP victory came alongside news of his new Williams deal.

facts.headline: Rupert Keegan dies
facts.detail: The 1970s F1 driver, known for capturing the grit and glamour of the era, died after a long illness.

facts.headline: Mansell is fined and banned for ignoring a black flag
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell overshot his pit box while leading, then continued despite the disqualification signal.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins the first US GP in a decade
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher overcame a late spin for his 42nd career victory.

facts.headline: Red Bull clinches its sixth Constructors' Championship
facts.detail: Max Verstappen's dominant Japanese GP victory secured the title with races to spare.

facts.headline: Rosberg wins his only title in a Las Vegas casino car park
facts.detail: Keke Rosberg's championship was decided at the Caesars Palace GP, held in the venue's parking lot.

facts.headline: Alonso becomes the youngest F1 champion at the time
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso, 24, clinched the title with third place at the Brazilian GP.

facts.headline: The Russian GP contract is terminated
facts.detail: F1 scrapped all future races in Russia following the invasion of Ukraine.

facts.headline: Prost becomes only the second man to win four titles
facts.detail: Alain Prost joined Fangio in the four-championship club with a Portuguese GP result.

facts.headline: Grosjean returns to an F1 cockpit five years after his fireball crash
facts.detail: Romain Grosjean drove a demonstration run for Haas at Mugello in an emotional comeback.

facts.headline: Herbert wins a chaotic European GP
facts.detail: Johnny Herbert's Stewart claimed victory in a race full of retirements.

facts.headline: Mansell breaks Senna's single-season win record
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's ninth win of 1992 surpassed Ayrton Senna's four-year-old mark.

facts.headline: Hakkinen takes a four-point title lead with one race left
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen's Luxembourg GP win set up a season-deciding finale against Schumacher.

facts.headline: Enzo Osella dies
facts.detail: The founder of the Osella team, who learned cars from the ground up in his family's garage, died at 86.

facts.headline: Mika Hakkinen is born
facts.detail: The double champion overcame a serious 1995 crash to become one of F1's most respected drivers.

facts.headline: Martin Donnelly survives a 140mph crash that ends his career
facts.detail: His Lotus disintegrated after hitting a barrier during Spanish GP practice.

facts.headline: Alonso's 'miracle' Singapore win is later revealed as a fix
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso's victory from 15th became infamous as part of the Crashgate scandal.

facts.headline: Barrichello wins by 0.011 seconds in a staged finish
facts.detail: A Ferrari team order gone slightly wrong produced one of F1's closest-ever margins at Indianapolis.

facts.headline: Mansell wins the inaugural Spanish GP at Catalunya despite a twisted ankle
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell overcame a football injury sustained days before the race.

facts.headline: John Foulston dies testing an IndyCar
facts.detail: The owner of Brands Hatch and other British circuits died in a crash at Silverstone.

facts.headline: Max Verstappen is born
facts.detail: Verstappen went on to become a multiple World Champion with over 70 race wins.

facts.headline: Hakkinen wins his final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen's US GP victory came in front of a 170,000-strong crowd.

facts.headline: Senna's retirement streak begins, gifting Prost the win
facts.detail: The first of three consecutive Senna retirements let Alain Prost win the Spanish GP.

facts.headline: Cliff Allison is born
facts.detail: The Ferrari driver mysteriously woke from a 16-day coma after a crash speaking only French, despite being English.

facts.headline: Spa is dropped from the 2006 calendar
facts.detail: Renovation delays at the Belgian circuit forced organizers to skip the race that year.

facts.headline: Cadillac unveils its first F1 livery
facts.detail: The reveal came during a Super Bowl commercial, introducing the manufacturer's debut look ahead of its season.

facts.headline: Jean-Pierre Jabouille is born
facts.detail: Jabouille scored the first-ever win by a turbocharged car at the 1979 French GP, driving for Renault.

facts.headline: Clark and Hill lead a British 1-2 at Watkins Glen
facts.detail: The Lotus pair kept the championship alive heading into the season's final race.

facts.headline: Schumacher takes his 91st and final F1 win
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Chinese GP victory drew him level with Alonso in the standings.

facts.headline: The modern-era British GP debuts at Silverstone
facts.detail: The 1948 race, run under new regulations, also marked the circuit's official opening.

facts.headline: Lauda clinches his second title with a cautious fourth place
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's measured drive at Watkins Glen secured the championship after his fiery 1976 crash.

facts.headline: Prost wins his second race in eight days
facts.detail: Alain Prost's Spanish GP win built a five-point lead over teammate Senna.

facts.headline: Hill completes a hat-trick of wins
facts.detail: Graham Hill's BRM held off Jim Clark at Watkins Glen for his third consecutive US GP victory.

facts.headline: Cevert wins the season finale
facts.detail: Francois Cevert capped a breakout season with victory at Watkins Glen.

facts.headline: Hunt closes to within eight points of Lauda
facts.detail: James Hunt's Canadian GP win kept the title fight alive with two races remaining.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi's win seals Rindt's posthumous title
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi's US GP victory ensured no rival could catch the late Jochen Rindt in the standings.

facts.headline: Denny Hulme dies of a heart attack while racing
facts.detail: The 1967 World Champion collapsed at the wheel during the Bathurst 1000 in Australia.

facts.headline: De Gaulle shelves plans for a national French F1 car
facts.detail: Economic stabilization measures scrapped the ambitious project.

facts.headline: Rindt wins at Watkins Glen, a year before tragedy struck both podium finishers
facts.detail: By the time F1 returned to the circuit, both Jochen Rindt and runner-up Piers Courage had died.

facts.headline: Lauda gives Ferrari its first-ever Watkins Glen win
facts.detail: Niki Lauda's fifth win of an already-clinched championship season came by 4.9 seconds.

facts.headline: Andrea de Cesaris dies in a motorcycle accident
facts.detail: The famously crash-prone F1 veteran died on a Rome motorway.

facts.headline: Francois Cevert is killed in practice at Watkins Glen
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's close friend and teammate died when his Tyrrell hit a barrier, devastating the paddock.

facts.headline: Fittipaldi secures his second title
facts.detail: Emerson Fittipaldi's championship was sealed when his last challenger retired at Watkins Glen.

facts.headline: Mansell calls his win 'the best day of my life'
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's European GP victory at Brands Hatch was an emotional breakthrough.

facts.headline: Villeneuve wins the wet season finale
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve beat Rene Arnoux by 48 seconds at Watkins Glen.

facts.headline: Prost sets up a title finale against Lauda
facts.detail: Alain Prost's European GP win, despite a spin, left the championship to be decided at the last race.

facts.headline: Verstappen clinches his third consecutive title
facts.detail: Max Verstappen secured the championship in Qatar after Perez's title hopes ended.

facts.headline: Lotus wins its first Grand Prix, overshadowed by tragedy
facts.detail: Colin Chapman's team's historic breakthrough came the same weekend as Wolfgang von Trips' fatal Italian GP crash.

facts.headline: Villeneuve becomes the first Canadian to win a home Grand Prix
facts.detail: Gilles Villeneuve triumphed for Ferrari at the inaugural Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.

facts.headline: Schumacher gives Ferrari its first title in over 20 years
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher beat Mika Hakkinen in a straight fight at the Japanese GP.

facts.headline: Raikkonen delivers one of F1's greatest comeback wins
facts.detail: Starting 17th, Kimi Raikkonen took the lead on the final lap of the Japanese GP.

facts.headline: Vettel clinches his second consecutive title
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel's third-place finish in Japan was enough to secure back-to-back championships.

facts.headline: Rosberg dominates at Suzuka
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg led start to finish, strengthening his championship bid.

facts.headline: Murray Walker is born
facts.detail: The legendary voice of F1 broadcasting left a rich commentary legacy spanning decades.

facts.headline: Schumacher qualifies on pole and wins on the same typhoon-hit day
facts.detail: Weather chaos at Suzuka forced qualifying to move to race day, a first in F1 history.

facts.headline: Hunt closes to within three points of Lauda
facts.detail: James Hunt's Watkins Glen win kept the dramatic title fight alive.

facts.headline: Hill is announced as Senna's new Williams teammate
facts.detail: Damon Hill admitted mixed emotions about partnering the forceful and motivated Ayrton Senna for 1994.

facts.headline: Alonso's frustration with rookie Hamilton boils into an FIA complaint
facts.detail: Tensions between the McLaren teammates led to an independent steward being sent to future races.

facts.headline: Hamilton extends his championship lead in Russia
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's win came as teammate Rosberg retired early from pole.

facts.headline: Schumacher sets up a winner-takes-all finale with Villeneuve
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Japanese GP win left the title to be decided at the final race.

facts.headline: Schumacher wins his sixth title, breaking Fangio's record
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's championship also marked his fourth title in five years.

facts.headline: Hamilton accuses Massa of deliberately crashing into him
facts.detail: The pair clashed fighting for position at a controversial Japanese GP.

facts.headline: Hill becomes F1's first second-generation champion
facts.detail: Damon Hill's Japanese GP win clinched the title, following father Graham Hill's two championships.

facts.headline: A dominant Schumacher masterclass is called a 'TV turn-off'
facts.detail: Critics panned the processional Ferrari 1-2 season finale as bad for the sport's spectacle.

facts.headline: Vettel extends his championship lead in Japan
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel's win came despite a strong early challenge from Romain Grosjean.

facts.headline: Schumacher's dominance sparks questions about the sport's health
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's season-ending Japanese GP win prompted debate over one-sided championships.

facts.headline: Gianpiero Lambiase is born
facts.detail: Lambiase became the calm, steady voice inside Max Verstappen's helmet as his Red Bull race engineer.

facts.headline: Gabriel Bortoleto is born
facts.detail: The karting prodigy went on to become a Formula 3 World Champion and F1 talent.

facts.headline: Piquet snatches the title from Prost at the final round
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet's second championship came at Prost's expense in South Africa.

facts.headline: Bruno Senna is born
facts.detail: The nephew of Ayrton Senna carried the family name into his own F1 career.

facts.headline: Craig Breedlove sets a new land speed record
facts.detail: Breedlove hit 468mph at Bonneville, edging past a rival's record set just a week before.

facts.headline: Schumacher returns from a ban to derail Hill's momentum
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's European GP win at Jerez came right after serving a two-race suspension.

facts.headline: Charles Leclerc is born
facts.detail: The Monegasque driver became one of the grid's elite talents at Ferrari.

facts.headline: Alonso and Renault seal a championship double
facts.detail: Fernando Alonso's Chinese GP win secured both the Drivers' and Constructors' titles.

facts.headline: Jones hands his title to Piquet in his farewell race
facts.detail: Alan Jones won the Caesars Palace GP in what he called his final race, as Piquet secured the championship.

facts.headline: Hakkinen retains his title after both Ferraris are disqualified
facts.detail: A post-race DQ in Malaysia handed Mika Hakkinen the championship for a second time.

facts.headline: Kimi Raikkonen is born
facts.detail: 'The Iceman' went on to win the 2007 World Championship with Ferrari.

facts.headline: Mansell wins big but leaves complaining about the stewards
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's 26-second Mexican GP victory came with lingering frustration over a rival's lack of penalty.

facts.headline: Button fulfills his boyhood dream of becoming champion
facts.detail: Jenson Button drove from 14th to fifth at the Brazilian GP to clinch the title.

facts.headline: Clemente Biondetti is born
facts.detail: One of the greatest sportscar racers ever, Biondetti won the Mille Miglia a then-unprecedented four times.

facts.headline: Hawthorn wins the title by a single point
facts.detail: Mike Hawthorn became Britain's first World Champion, edging out Stirling Moss by the narrowest of margins.

facts.headline: Ascari wins the Italian GP by over 16 minutes
facts.detail: Antonio Ascari's Alfa Romeo demolished the field in one of the most dominant wins of the era.

facts.headline: Stewart clinches the title finishing fourth
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's championship was already secured before the season finale began.

facts.headline: Gunnar Nilsson dies of cancer at 29
facts.detail: The 1977 Belgian GP winner's rare talent had made him a rising star before his early death.

facts.headline: Senna and Mansell head into a title-deciding Japanese GP
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell needed a win to keep his championship hopes alive against Ayrton Senna.

facts.headline: Williams confirms Rosberg for its second race seat
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg's signing was reported ahead of the team's official announcement.

facts.headline: Lauda wins his third title by half a point
facts.detail: Niki Lauda edged teammate Alain Prost in the closest championship margin in F1 history.

facts.headline: Senna and Prost collide again to decide the title
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna deliberately crashed into Alain Prost at the first corner of the Japanese GP to clinch the championship.

facts.headline: Raikkonen wins his only title by a single point
facts.detail: Kimi Raikkonen's dramatic Interlagos triumph beat both McLarens of Hamilton and Alonso.

facts.headline: Prost clinches the title after a controversial Suzuka collision
facts.detail: Alain Prost's championship was secured amid one of F1's most disputed clashes with teammate Senna.

facts.headline: Hulme clinches his only World Championship
facts.detail: Denny Hulme's third-place finish in Mexico was enough to seal the title.

facts.headline: Schumacher's iconic Ferrari career ends
facts.detail: A fourth-place finish in Brazil marked the last race of Michael Schumacher's first F1 career.

facts.headline: The Spanish GP is cancelled following the Le Mans disaster
facts.detail: New safety regulations sparked by the tragedy reshaped the calendar.

facts.headline: Hunt returns to Fuji for another triumph
facts.detail: James Hunt's Japanese GP win came a year after his dramatic title victory at the same circuit.

facts.headline: Alex Zanardi is born
facts.detail: Zanardi later survived a horrific crash and returned to competition as a Paralympic champion.

facts.headline: Lauda withdraws from the rain-soaked title decider at Fuji
facts.detail: Niki Lauda pulled out of the race just weeks after his near-fatal Nurburgring crash, handing Hunt the title.

facts.headline: Honda scores its first-ever F1 win
facts.detail: Richie Ginther's Mexican GP victory was also the first for a non-European manufacturer.

facts.headline: Jo Siffert dies in a non-championship race
facts.detail: A suspension failure caused his fatal crash at Brands Hatch.

facts.headline: Hamilton breaks Schumacher's all-time win record
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's 92nd career victory at the Portuguese GP surpassed Michael Schumacher's long-standing mark.

facts.headline: One of F1's most dramatic title deciders unfolds in Mexico
facts.detail: Three drivers arrived with a shot at the championship in a chaotic season finale.

facts.headline: Patrese wins his final Grand Prix
facts.detail: Riccardo Patrese's Japanese GP win was the last by an Italian driver for over a decade.

facts.headline: Prost wins one of F1's most thrilling season finales
facts.detail: Alain Prost beat the Williams pair of Mansell and Piquet in a dramatic three-way title battle.

facts.headline: Villeneuve clinches the title after a collision with Schumacher
facts.detail: Jacques Villeneuve overcame Michael Schumacher's controversial attempt to take him out at Jerez.

facts.headline: Norris leads every lap in Mexico City
facts.detail: Lando Norris's dominant drive delivered a commanding victory.

facts.headline: Clark equals Fangio's single-season win record
facts.detail: Jim Clark's sixth win of an already-clinched title season came at the inaugural Mexican GP.

facts.headline: Schumacher meets a 16-year-old Lewis Hamilton
facts.detail: The pair crossed paths at a karting event in Schumacher's hometown, with Schumacher praising the young talent.

facts.headline: Ferrari threatens to quit F1 over engine standardization
facts.detail: The proposal to standardize engines and transmissions from 2010 sparked a major power struggle.

facts.headline: Bernie Ecclestone is born
facts.detail: The future F1 commercial rights holder began his working life selling second-hand bicycles.

facts.headline: Fangio wins his first title
facts.detail: Juan Manuel Fangio's Alfa Romeo team used clever tactics, including dummy fuel tanks, to secure the championship.

facts.headline: Patrese is acquitted in Peterson's death
facts.detail: A Milan court cleared Riccardo Patrese of manslaughter charges over the 1978 Italian GP crash.

facts.headline: Schumacher matches Mansell's single-season win record
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's ninth win of the year also sealed Benetton's Constructors' title.

facts.headline: Hamilton clinches his fourth title with two races to spare
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's championship victory came at the Mexican GP.

facts.headline: Verstappen sets a new single-season win record
facts.detail: Max Verstappen's 16th victory of 2023 broke his own previous mark.

facts.headline: Nino Farina is born
facts.detail: Farina made history winning the first-ever F1 World Championship in 1950, known for his aggressive style.

facts.headline: Senna wins his first World Championship
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's Japanese GP victory, amid a collision with Prost, clinched the first of his three titles.

facts.headline: Ferrari's Malaysian disqualification is overturned before the finale
facts.detail: The FIA's reversal positioned Eddie Irvine as title favorite heading into Japan.

facts.headline: Hakkinen ends Irvine's best title shot
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen's Japanese GP win at Suzuka secured his second championship.

facts.headline: Derek Bell is born
facts.detail: Bell won Le Mans five times, though his F1 career with Ferrari was comparatively brief.

facts.headline: Sebastien Buemi is born
facts.detail: Buemi entered F1 through the Red Bull Young Driver Program, replacing Vettel at Toro Rosso.

facts.headline: Ricardo Rodriguez dies qualifying for his home race
facts.detail: The 20-year-old Mexican talent crashed fatally trying to impress the crowd after Ferrari opted out of the race.

facts.headline: Hakkinen wins his first World Championship
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen's flag-to-flag Japanese GP victory also secured McLaren's first title in years.

facts.headline: Irvine is fired over the phone
facts.detail: Jaguar boss Niki Lauda dismissed Eddie Irvine abruptly, ending a turbulent tenure.

facts.headline: Alan Jones is born
facts.detail: Jones won the 1980 title and gave Williams its first-ever Constructors' Championship.

facts.headline: Hamilton wins his first title on the final lap
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton needed fifth place at the Brazilian GP and secured it with the last corner of the season.

facts.headline: Mauro Forghieri dies
facts.detail: One of the greatest engineers in F1 history, Forghieri was a defining figure at Ferrari for decades.

facts.headline: Hill wins his second World Championship
facts.detail: Graham Hill's decisive Mexican GP win narrowly beat rival Jackie Stewart.

facts.headline: Rosberg wins his Williams farewell race
facts.detail: Keke Rosberg triumphed in scorching heat at the inaugural Australian GP in Adelaide.

facts.headline: F1 holds its shortest race, a record that stood for 30 years
facts.detail: Torrential rain cut the Australian GP to just 14 laps before the 2021 Belgian GP took the record.

facts.headline: Piquet wins as Mansell drives his final race for Ferrari
facts.detail: Nelson Piquet held off Nigel Mansell's fierce challenge at the Australian GP.

facts.headline: Murray Walker criticizes F1 drivers as too bland
facts.detail: The legendary commentator argued the sport lacked drivers willing to speak their minds.

facts.headline: Raikkonen wins his first race back in F1
facts.detail: Kimi Raikkonen's Abu Dhabi victory for Lotus was his first since 2009.

facts.headline: Boutsen wins a chaotic rain-hit Australian GP
facts.detail: Thirteen of 25 starters crashed out before the race was stopped early.

facts.headline: Andrea de Adamich dies
facts.detail: The versatile Italian driver, celebrated across F1, touring cars, and endurance racing, died at 84.

facts.headline: Verstappen dominates both sprint and Grand Prix in Brazil
facts.detail: Max Verstappen further cemented his record-breaking season.

facts.headline: Peter Collins is born
facts.detail: Collins became a prominent Ferrari driver of the 1950s before his death at the German GP.

facts.headline: Jack McGrath dies on his announced final race day
facts.detail: The 'King of the Hot Rods' was killed in a crash after already deciding to retire.

facts.headline: Hill wins a rain-drenched Japanese GP to keep his title hopes alive
facts.detail: Damon Hill's victory extended his championship pursuit against Schumacher.

facts.headline: Senna wins the 41st and final race of his career
facts.detail: Ayrton Senna's Australian GP victory closed out six years with McLaren.

facts.headline: Vladimir Putin takes the wheel of an F1 car
facts.detail: The Russian prime minister drove a modified Prost at a private test near St. Petersburg.

facts.headline: Vettel wins in Brazil
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel started second and beat teammate Webber to victory.

facts.headline: Mansell's intended final race turns sour
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell's collision with Ayrton Senna while battling for the lead soured what was meant to be a celebratory farewell.

facts.headline: Newey joins Red Bull from McLaren
facts.detail: The renowned aerodynamicist's move became one of F1's most consequential technical hires.

facts.headline: Hill disputes his salary before the championship decider
facts.detail: Damon Hill's £300,000 retainer paled next to teammate Mansell's reported £950,000.

facts.headline: Renault is embroiled in a McLaren data scandal
