facts.detail: Confidential information transferred via a moving engineer sparked a major espionage controversy.

facts.headline: Fallout from the Mosley libel trial continues
facts.detail: A tabloid editor accused the presiding judge of quietly imposing a privacy law through his rulings.

facts.headline: Eddie Irvine is born
facts.detail: Irvine nearly won the 1999 World Championship, one of F1's more colorful characters.

facts.headline: Lucien Bianchi is born
facts.detail: Bianchi's F1 career preceded a family tragedy decades later when descendant Jules Bianchi died from injuries at the 2014 Japanese GP.

facts.headline: Alexandre Darracq is born
facts.detail: Darracq became a major figure in the early automotive industry, later selling his business to fund other ventures.

facts.headline: Maria Teresa de Filippis is born
facts.detail: De Filippis became F1's first female driver, breaking barriers in a male-dominated sport.

facts.headline: Vittorio Brambilla, 'the Monza Gorilla', is born
facts.detail: Brambilla is remembered for his sole win, famously ending with a celebratory crash.

facts.headline: Schumacher signs a massive Ferrari extension
facts.detail: The deal, reportedly worth over $25 million a year, committed Michael Schumacher through 1999.

facts.headline: Peter Whitehead becomes Ferrari's first F1 privateer
facts.detail: Whitehead convinced Enzo Ferrari to sell him a car, leading the 1950 French GP at one point.

facts.headline: Hill wins his 14th Grand Prix at Adelaide's final race
facts.detail: Damon Hill's win came with the title already sealed by Schumacher.

facts.headline: Ross Brawn is named Honda's team principal
facts.detail: The appointment set in motion the chain of events that led to Brawn GP's title-winning 2009 season.

facts.headline: Schumacher's controversial collision with Hill clinches the title
facts.detail: A contested crash between the title rivals at the Australian GP decided the championship.

facts.headline: Hakkinen is discharged after a near-fatal crash
facts.detail: Mika Hakkinen left intensive care following a high-speed practice accident weeks earlier.

facts.headline: Prost wins his 35th race despite handling issues
facts.detail: Alain Prost battled debris damage while teammate Senna suffered a malfunction.

facts.headline: Tommy Milton is born
facts.detail: Milton became the first two-time Indianapolis 500 winner despite limited vision that once led to his rejection from racing.

facts.headline: Eliseo Salazar is born
facts.detail: Salazar is best remembered for his televised confrontation with Nelson Piquet after their 1982 German GP collision.

facts.headline: Rosberg and Piquet Jr. are lined up for Williams testing
facts.detail: Both drivers were set to be evaluated as potential test drivers for 2004.

facts.headline: A memorial service is held for Ken Tyrrell
facts.detail: Guildford Cathedral hosted a thanksgiving service for the influential team owner.

facts.headline: Red Bull is confirmed as Jaguar's new owner
facts.detail: Ford sold the struggling team, reshaping the grid heading into 2005.

facts.headline: Ecclestone calls for lifetime bans over racial abuse
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone's comments followed criticism of his own initial downplaying of abuse directed at Hamilton.

facts.headline: Tazio Nuvolari is born
facts.detail: Widely hailed as one of the greatest drivers ever, Nuvolari didn't start racing seriously until his 30s.

facts.headline: Scuderia Ferrari is founded
facts.detail: The team initially raced Alfa Romeos before Enzo Ferrari built his own manufacturer.

facts.headline: Christian Horner is born
facts.detail: Horner led Red Bull Racing from 2005, guiding the team to multiple World Championships.

facts.headline: Montoya's move to McLaren is confirmed
facts.detail: Juan Pablo Montoya would leave Williams for McLaren starting in 2005.

facts.headline: Brundle announces he's joining the BBC
facts.detail: Martin Brundle became a Formula 1 commentator for the network in 2009.

facts.headline: Gasly and Sainz score their first-ever podiums
facts.detail: Both drivers celebrated career milestones behind race winner Verstappen in Brazil.

facts.headline: F1's longest-serving journalist dies
facts.detail: Gerard 'Jabby' Crombac had covered the sport since before the World Championship began in 1950.

facts.headline: The Las Vegas GP hosts F1's 1,100th championship race
facts.detail: The new street circuit marked a major milestone for the sport.

facts.headline: Button reveals he almost missed his F1 debut
facts.detail: Williams technical director Patrick Head initially leaned toward a different rookie before choosing Button.

facts.headline: Raikkonen announces a break from Formula One
facts.detail: Kimi Raikkonen's planned sabbatical, with uncertainty about returning, ended up lasting two seasons.

facts.headline: BAR's team boss departs after Honda's stake purchase
facts.detail: Dave Richards left following Honda's $150 million investment in the team.

facts.headline: Al Keller dies from Champ Car injuries
facts.detail: The veteran of the Indianapolis 500 died from a crash at the Arizona State Fairgrounds.

facts.headline: Gunnar Nilsson is born
facts.detail: Nilsson's highlight was a rain-soaked win at the 1977 Belgian GP; he died of cancer at 29.

facts.headline: Stefan Bellof is born
facts.detail: Considered a future world champion, Bellof died in a 1985 sportscar crash at Spa.

facts.headline: Ecclestone's wife announces their divorce
facts.detail: Slavica Ecclestone's decision ended a 24-year marriage, catching Bernie by surprise.

facts.headline: Jacques Laffite is born
facts.detail: Laffite became the first Frenchman to win a World Championship race, at the 1977 Swedish GP.

facts.headline: Lauda resigns as his airline's CEO amid financial scrutiny
facts.detail: Niki Lauda stepped down from Lauda Air following reports of irregularities.

facts.headline: Fisichella has his license confiscated for speeding
facts.detail: Giancarlo Fisichella was clocked at more than double the limit in Rome.

facts.headline: Rosberg edges Hamilton for pole at the title decider
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg's Abu Dhabi pole set up a tense championship-deciding finale.

facts.headline: F1 holds its first-ever Qatar Grand Prix
facts.detail: The Lusail circuit hosted a late addition to the calendar.

facts.headline: Ross Brawn is born
facts.detail: Brawn became one of F1's most successful strategic minds, building championship-winning teams across multiple eras.

facts.headline: F1 controversially awards double points for the first time
facts.detail: The season-finale rule change at Abu Dhabi drew criticism from fans and drivers alike.

facts.headline: Verstappen clinches his fourth consecutive title
facts.detail: Max Verstappen's fifth-place finish in Las Vegas was enough to secure the championship.

facts.headline: Minardi is rebranded as Toro Rosso
facts.detail: The beloved underdog team's final race came before a Red Bull takeover transformed it.

facts.headline: Hamilton is confirmed as Alonso's McLaren teammate
facts.detail: At just 21 and without ever driving an F1 car, Lewis Hamilton's promotion set up one of F1's fiercest rivalries.

facts.headline: Vettel wins his ninth consecutive race
facts.detail: Sebastian Vettel's Brazilian GP victory capped a dominant record-setting season.

facts.headline: Charlie Whiting officiates his final race
facts.detail: The respected Race Director passed away suddenly before the following season began.

facts.headline: Zanardi tests an F1 car five years after losing his legs
facts.detail: Alex Zanardi posted impressive times in a specially modified BMW Sauber.

facts.headline: Button wins the final race of his career
facts.detail: Jenson Button's Brazilian GP victory was his 15th and last.

facts.headline: The first American Grand Prize is held
facts.detail: Louis Wagner's Fiat won the road race in Savannah, Georgia.

facts.headline: Desire Wilson is born
facts.detail: Wilson remains the only woman to win an F1-spec race, taking victory in the British Aurora F1 series in 1980.

facts.headline: The FIA approves flame-resistant driver clothing
facts.detail: The overdue safety measure came after years of severe burn injuries in the sport.

facts.headline: The FIA unveils a record 17-race calendar for 1976
facts.detail: The expanded schedule added two US races and a new event.

facts.headline: Giancarlo Baghetti dies
facts.detail: Baghetti holds the unique record of winning his debut World Championship race.

facts.headline: Webber wins his only race of the season
facts.detail: Mark Webber's Brazilian GP victory was his sole win in an otherwise difficult year.

facts.headline: Surtees signs with Honda
facts.detail: The 1964 champion left Ferrari mid-season amid a dispute before joining the Japanese manufacturer.

facts.headline: Frank Williams dies
facts.detail: The legendary founder of Williams F1 dedicated his life to the team he built from nothing.

facts.headline: Hamilton's first F1 test ends after two laps
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's McLaren broke down early in his maiden test at Barcelona.

facts.headline: Graham Hill dies in a plane crash, killing his entire team
facts.detail: The double champion's light aircraft crashed in fog, also killing promising young driver Tony Brise and four others.

facts.headline: Massa returns to karting after his near-fatal crash
facts.detail: Felipe Massa raced alongside Schumacher four months after his life-threatening Hungarian GP injury.

facts.headline: Raikkonen announces his F1 return
facts.detail: Kimi Raikkonen would rejoin the grid with the team that became Lotus F1 for 2012.

facts.headline: Raikkonen apologizes for a wild nightclub photo scandal
facts.detail: Photos surfaced of Kimi Raikkonen partying and collapsing atop an inflatable dolphin in Gran Canaria.

facts.headline: Hakkinen briefly returns to the cockpit for testing
facts.detail: The double champion completed 77 laps helping McLaren with winter testing.

facts.headline: Mika Salo is born
facts.detail: Salo's 111-race F1 career included two podium finishes despite a career setback from a drink-driving conviction.

facts.headline: F1 holds its first December race since 1963
facts.detail: The season-ending Abu Dhabi GP marked a rare calendar quirk, pushing the finale later than usual.

facts.headline: Hamilton tests positive for COVID-19
facts.detail: The reigning champion was sidelined from the Sakhir GP after already having clinched the title.

facts.headline: Norris's title bid is hit by a controversial penalty
facts.detail: A dramatic duel with Verstappen at the Qatar GP ended in Norris's favor being overturned.

facts.headline: Ken Tyrrell sells his team to British American Racing
facts.detail: The iconic Tyrrell outfit, which had debuted in 1968, changed hands after nearly three decades.

facts.headline: Rosberg retires days after winning his first title
facts.detail: Nico Rosberg's shock announcement stunned the motorsport world just after beating Hamilton to the championship.

facts.headline: Red Bull confirms its 2026 driver lineup shake-up
facts.detail: Isack Hadjar was paired with Verstappen while Yuki Tsunoda lost his seat.

facts.headline: Ecclestone strikes a deal with Sylvester Stallone to bring F1 back to the US
facts.detail: The Hollywood star planned to film scenes during practice sessions as part of the push.

facts.headline: The EU announces a sweeping tobacco advertising ban in sports
facts.detail: The decision, after nine years of negotiation, would reshape F1's sponsorship landscape.

facts.headline: Sauber announces its return to F1 for 2010
facts.detail: The team re-entered the sport after BMW's withdrawal left it without a place on the grid.

facts.headline: Mansell is caught speeding in his new Bentley
facts.detail: Nigel Mansell was pulled over doing 92mph in a 70 zone shortly after buying the £233,000 car.

facts.headline: Ferrari executives hold a private audience with the Pope
facts.detail: Luca di Montezemolo and Piero Ferrari met Pope Benedict XVI at the Vatican.

facts.headline: Raikkonen's move to rallying is confirmed
facts.detail: A potential Ferrari-to-McLaren switch fell through over salary terms, sending Kimi Raikkonen to the WRC instead.

facts.headline: Graham Hill's funeral draws thousands of mourners
facts.detail: Over 2,000 attended the service at St Albans Abbey, with as many listening outside.

facts.headline: McLaren admits falsifying information in the Spygate scandal
facts.detail: The team's damaging reversal came before an FIA hearing into Renault's alleged data misuse.

facts.headline: Honda announces its shock withdrawal from F1
facts.detail: Citing the global financial crisis, Honda's exit set the stage for the Brawn GP takeover.

facts.headline: Keke Rosberg is born
facts.detail: The 1982 World Champion won his title with just a single Grand Prix victory that season.

facts.headline: Clay Regazzoni dies in a road accident
facts.detail: The former F1 race winner was killed near Parma at age 67.

facts.headline: Renault avoids punishment despite a guilty Spygate verdict
facts.detail: The decision shocked observers after McLaren had been fined £50 million earlier that year.

facts.headline: Robert Kubica is born
facts.detail: Poland's first F1 driver became the 99th different race winner with his 2008 Canadian GP victory.

facts.headline: A tobacco-ban delay scandal embarrasses the government and Ecclestone
facts.detail: Reports alleged the Labour Party sought to delay advertising restrictions to benefit F1.

facts.headline: A potential breakaway championship is thwarted
facts.detail: Williams joined Ferrari, Red Bull, and Midland in committing to the existing championship structure.

facts.headline: Irvine judges the Miss World competition
facts.detail: Eddie Irvine found an unusual off-track audience shortly after his title-challenging season.

facts.headline: A traffic officer doubts Ralf Schumacher's identity after a speeding stop
facts.detail: Caught doing 80mph in a 50 zone, Schumacher was met with disbelief from police in Austria.

facts.headline: Reutemann tests a modern Ferrari decades after his career
facts.detail: The 1970s Ferrari star called driving the F2004 an unforgettable experience.

facts.headline: Senna narrowly avoids a ban for striking Irvine
facts.detail: The FIA handed Ayrton Senna a suspended sentence following a post-race altercation with Eddie Irvine.

facts.headline: Senna's crash investigation findings go public
facts.detail: Lead investigator Professor Enrico Lorenzini's report reignited debate over the cause of Ayrton Senna's fatal accident.

facts.headline: Lotus announces its entry into Formula One
facts.detail: Colin Chapman revealed the team's first F1 car, the Type 12, for the 1958 season.

facts.headline: An arrest warrant is issued for Irvine over a speeding charge
facts.detail: Eddie Irvine failed to appear in a London court over a scooter speeding incident.

facts.headline: Ecclestone floats a London street Grand Prix
facts.detail: Bernie Ecclestone expressed interest in staging a race through the capital's streets.

facts.headline: The Hill team loses its main sponsor after Graham Hill's death
facts.detail: Tobacco company WD & HO Wills' withdrawal effectively doomed the team he founded.

facts.headline: China's inaugural Grand Prix is postponed by a year
facts.detail: The FIA determined the Zhuhai circuit needed more preparation time.

facts.headline: Schumacher races a fighter jet
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's Ferrari F2003 challenged a Eurofighter Typhoon in a unique publicity stunt.

facts.headline: Emerson Fittipaldi is born
facts.detail: The two-time World Champion won titles in 1972 and 1974 across an 11-year F1 career.

facts.headline: Stewart becomes only the second F1 driver named BBC Sports Personality of the Year
facts.detail: Jackie Stewart's honor came shortly after his retirement as a three-time champion.

facts.headline: Brabham runs out of fuel in sight of the finish line
facts.detail: Jack Brabham had to push his car home at the season-ending US GP at Sebring.

facts.headline: Mansell wins BBC Sports Personality as Williams announces his replacement
facts.detail: Damon Hill was confirmed to replace the newly-crowned champion Nigel Mansell for the following season.

facts.headline: ITV takes over F1 broadcasting from the BBC
facts.detail: The switch ended the BBC's long-standing coverage, shocking British fans.

facts.headline: McLaren issues an unreserved apology to end the Spygate saga
facts.detail: Team boss Martin Whitmarsh expressed 'sincere regret' in a formal letter to the FIA and Ferrari.

facts.headline: A disastrous Indianapolis opening leads to brick paving
facts.detail: The poor original track surface caused fatal accidents, prompting the famous brick resurfacing.

facts.headline: Kovalainen is announced as Hamilton's new McLaren teammate
facts.detail: Heikki Kovalainen replaced Fernando Alonso after his turbulent single season at the team.

facts.headline: Antonio Giovinazzi is born
facts.detail: Giovinazzi made his F1 debut with Sauber at the 2017 Australian GP.

facts.headline: Clay Regazzoni's death is mourned across the sport
facts.detail: The former F1 race winner died in a road accident near Parma.

facts.headline: Marco Andretti becomes F1's first third-generation test driver
facts.detail: The grandson of 1978 champion Mario Andretti made history with his test outing.

facts.headline: The Belgian GP is cancelled over tobacco advertising rules
facts.detail: Hopes that local government would resolve the restrictions in time faded.

facts.headline: Colin Chapman dies
facts.detail: The Lotus founder, whose innovations reshaped F1 car design, died of a heart attack at 54.

facts.headline: Henry Taylor is born
facts.detail: Taylor's best F1 result was fourth place at the 1960 French GP before he moved into team management.

facts.headline: Fears grow of a team boycott over the Senna manslaughter charges
facts.detail: Manslaughter charges against Frank Williams and five others over Ayrton Senna's death threatened the Italian GP.

facts.headline: Toyota unveils its F1 car after one of the longest development phases ever
facts.detail: The TF102's launch capped years of preparation for the manufacturer's entry.

facts.headline: The first recognized land speed record is set
facts.detail: Count Gaston de Chasseloup-Laubat's electric Jeantaud hit 39mph at Acheres, France.

facts.headline: Vijay Mallya is born
facts.detail: The Indian billionaire later owned and managed the Force India F1 team.

facts.headline: BAR unveils its new car a day after Toyota's launch
facts.detail: The BAR 004's reveal came amid a significant leadership shakeup at the team.

facts.headline: Onofre Marimon is born
facts.detail: Marimon became the first driver to die during a World Championship race weekend, at the 1954 German GP.

facts.headline: Alonso announces his move to McLaren
facts.detail: The reigning Renault champion called his 2007 switch 'a new beginning' and 'a tremendous challenge.'

facts.headline: Ferrari's secret $80 million bonus deal is revealed
facts.detail: The FIA faced embarrassment over the special Constructors' Championship agreement.

facts.headline: Karl Wendlinger is born
facts.detail: Wendlinger raced 42 Grands Prix before a serious 1994 Monaco practice crash affected his career.

facts.headline: Senna secretly tests an IndyCar
facts.detail: Frustrated by Williams' F1 dominance, Ayrton Senna briefly considered a switch to American racing.

facts.headline: Lorenzo Bandini is born
facts.detail: Bandini won one Grand Prix before dying from injuries sustained in his fiery 1967 Monaco crash.

facts.headline: The film Grand Prix premieres in the US
facts.detail: James Garner starred in the racing drama, praised for its authentic race footage.

facts.headline: Gary Hocking dies practicing, having switched to cars believing them safer
facts.detail: The former motorcycle world champion was killed ahead of the Natal GP.

facts.headline: Pierre Levegh is born
facts.detail: Levegh's car caused the catastrophic 1955 Le Mans disaster, motorsport's deadliest-ever accident.

facts.headline: Coulthard is annoyed at being misclassified as English in a video game
facts.detail: A new F1 Nintendo game grouped the Scottish driver among England's roster.

facts.headline: Super Aguri gets the green light to join F1
facts.detail: Former driver Aguri Suzuki's team secured late approval from the other teams.

facts.headline: Michele Alboreto is born
facts.detail: Alboreto won five races across 194 starts, most notably during his time at Ferrari.

facts.headline: Schumacher announces his F1 return
facts.detail: The seven-time champion confirmed his highly anticipated comeback for the 2010 season.

facts.headline: Prince Bira of Thailand is remembered
facts.detail: Bira was the first Southeast Asian driver to compete in F1, racing 19 World Championship Grands Prix.

facts.headline: John Cooper dies
facts.detail: The Cooper Car Company co-founder pioneered the rear-engine revolution that transformed F1 car design.

facts.headline: Howden Ganley is born
facts.detail: Ganley moved from mechanic to F1 driver, debuting at the 1971 South African GP.

facts.headline: Giancarlo Baghetti is born
facts.detail: Baghetti holds the unique F1 record of winning his debut World Championship race.

facts.headline: Wilson Fittipaldi is born on Christmas Day
facts.detail: The elder brother of two-time champion Emerson Fittipaldi had a less illustrious F1 career of his own.

facts.headline: Denis Jenkinson is born
facts.detail: Jenkinson became one of F1's most iconic journalists as Motor Sport magazine's longtime correspondent.

facts.headline: Adrian Newey is born
facts.detail: Widely regarded as F1's greatest-ever designer, Newey's chassis have won more than a dozen World Championships.

facts.headline: Trevor Taylor is born
facts.detail: Taylor's best F1 result was a second place at the 1962 Dutch GP.

facts.headline: Hans Stuck is born
facts.detail: The prolific pre-war driver earned legendary status as a hill climb specialist with Auto Union.

facts.headline: Frentzen signs a surprise deal with Arrows
facts.detail: Heinz-Harald Frentzen's one-year contract came after being let go by Jordan mid-season.

facts.headline: The season's delayed finale is held in South Africa
facts.detail: The 1963 championship's final race came a full two months after the previous round.

facts.headline: David Murray is born
facts.detail: Murray became a driver-turned-team-founder, later establishing the famed Ecurie Ecosse outfit.

facts.headline: Philippe Etancelin is born
facts.detail: The wealthy farmer became one of the 'over-50s gang' racing at F1's inaugural championship.

facts.headline: Schumacher suffers a severe head injury skiing
facts.detail: Michael Schumacher's accident in the French Alps led to a life-altering recovery.

facts.headline: Mike Beuttler dies from AIDS complications
facts.detail: The privateer F1 driver of the early 1970s died in the US.

facts.headline: Gil de Ferran dies
facts.detail: The two-time Champ Car champion and Indianapolis 500 winner was a prominent motorsport figure.

facts.headline: Prost calls modern F1 drivers 'trained monkeys'
facts.detail: The four-time champion criticized drivers for simply following engineers' instructions rather than racing on instinct.

facts.headline: Spence is invited to replace Clark at Lotus after his death
facts.detail: Colin Chapman turned to Mike Spence following Jim Clark's fatal accident earlier that year.

facts.headline: Guy Edwards is born
facts.detail: Edwards became known for his bravery helping rescue Niki Lauda from his burning car at the Nurburgring.

facts.headline: Land speed legend Malcolm Campbell dies
facts.detail: Sir Malcolm Campbell passed away at his Reigate home at 63.

facts.headline: Frank Williams is knighted
facts.detail: The Times described his career as combining ruthlessness with remarkable loyalty and achievement.

facts.headline: Hamilton becomes the only F1 driver knighted while still competing
facts.detail: Lewis Hamilton's knighthood came in the New Year's Honours list.
